### 1. Case Header, Cast of Characters & Procedural Posture
**Concise Recognizable Title: In Re: Justice Demetrio Demetria** (2001)
**Full Official Caption:** In Re: Derogatory News Items Charging Court of Appeals Associate Justice Demetrio Demetria with Interference on Behalf of a Suspected Drug Queen: Court of Appeals Associate Justice Demetrio G. Demetria, Respondent.
**Citation & Metadata:** A.M. No. 00-7-09-CA | March 27, 2001 | 407 Phil. 671 | **Per Curiam** | En Banc (Davide, Jr., **C.J.**, Bellosillo, Melo, Vitug, Kapunan, Mendoza, Panganiban, Quisumbing, Pardo, Buena, Gonzaga-Reyes, Ynares-Santiago, De Leon, Jr., and Sandoval-Gutierrez, **JJ.**, concurring; Puno, **J.**, on official business abroad; no separate opinions).
**Key Parties & Roles (The Cast):**
**Respondent:** Court of Appeals Associate Justice Demetrio G. Demetria (former Department of Justice [DOJ] Undersecretary and Acting Secretary).
**Prosecution Witnesses / Informants:** Chief State Prosecutor (CSP) Jovencito R. Zuño (DOJ); State Prosecutor (SP) Pablo C. Formaran III (DOJ Task Force on Anti-Narcotics Cases); Agnes P. Tuason (Secretary to SP Formaran III); Jose H. Afalla (DOJ employee).
**Investigating Officer & Court Prosecutor:** Retired Supreme Court Associate Justice Carolina C. Griño-Aquino (Investigating Justice); Court Administrator Alfredo L. Benipayo (designated Prosecutor).
**Other Key Persons in the Trial Record:** Yu Yuk Lai (alias Sze Yuk Lai, suspected Chinese "drug queen" detained for non-bailable drug trafficking); Go Teng Kok (President of the Philippine Amateur Track and Field Association [PATAFA], friend of Yu Yuk Lai); Atty. Reinerio Paas (private lawyer of Go Teng Kok and close friend of Justice Demetria); Judge Manuel T. Muro (Pairing Judge, RTC Manila, Branch 53); Judge Perfecto A.S. Laguio, Jr. (Presiding Judge, RTC Manila, Branch 18).
**How the Case Reached the Supreme Court:** Initiated **sua sponte** by the Supreme Court En Banc through a formal administrative inquiry under its constitutional disciplinary authority over lower-court justices, triggered by a Memorandum dated July 21, 2000 issued by Chief Justice Hilario G. Davide, Jr. directing Justice Demetria to comment on widespread national newspaper reports accusing him of exerting undue pressure on DOJ prosecutors to favor a detained drug suspect.
### 2. Syllabus Topic Grouping, Codal Provision & Factual Trigger
**Primary Topic Hierarchy:** Constitutional Law → The Judicial Department → Disciplinary Power over Lower-Court Justices and Judges (Article VIII, Section 6 and Section 11, 1987 Constitution).
**Secondary Topic Hierarchy:** Legal & Judicial Ethics → Code of Judicial Conduct → Canon 2, Rule 2.04 (Improper Influence on Pending Litigation).
**Full Text of Governing Constitutional & Regulatory Provisions:**
**Article VIII, Section 6, 1987 Philippine Constitution:**
"The Supreme Court shall have administrative supervision over all courts and the personnel thereof."
**Article VIII, Section 11, 1987 Philippine Constitution:**
"The Members of the Supreme Court and judges of lower courts shall hold office during good behavior until they reach the age of seventy years or become incapacitated to discharge the duties of their office. **The Supreme Court en banc shall have the power to discipline judges of lower courts, or order their dismissal by a vote of a majority of the Members who actually took part in the deliberations on the issues in the case and voted thereon.**"
**Rule 2.04, Canon 2, Code of Judicial Conduct:**
"**A judge shall refrain from influencing in any manner the outcome of litigation or dispute pending before another court or administrative agency.**"
**Factual Trigger:** Court of Appeals Associate Justice Demetrio Demetria personally went to the DOJ office of trial prosecutor SP Formaran III alongside Go Teng Kok to intercede on behalf of accused drug trafficker Yu Yuk Lai by urging Formaran to withdraw his pending Motion to Inhibit Judge Manuel Muro, and followed up this personal visit with an explicit telephone call to Chief State Prosecutor Jovencito Zuño requesting him to instruct Formaran to withdraw said motion so Judge Muro could resolve the accused's demurrer to evidence.
### 3. Chronological Facts Storyboard
**December 9, 1998:** SP Pablo C. Formaran III files an Information before RTC Manila, Branch 18 (presided by Judge Perfecto A.S. Laguio, Jr.) charging Yu Yuk Lai and Kenneth Monceda with violation of Section 15, Article III of R.A. No. 6425, as amended, for selling and delivering approximately 3 kilograms of **shabu**. Both are held without bail at Camp Crame.
**June 25, 1999:** Yu Yuk Lai files a Petition for Bail claiming the prosecution's evidence of guilt is not strong.
**November 10, 1999:** Upon learning that Yu Yuk Lai is regularly seen gambling at the Heritage Hotel and Holiday Inn Pavilion casinos, SP Formaran III files an **Urgent Ex-Parte Motion to Transfer the Detention of the Accused to the City Jail**. Judge Laguio grants it immediately and transfers the accused to the Manila City Jail.
**January 18, 2000:** Judge Laguio denies Yu Yuk Lai's petition for bail, finding the unrebutted evidence strong and sufficient to warrant conviction.
**January 28, 2000:** Accused file a Joint Motion for Inhibition against Judge Laguio. Though finding the motion unmeritorious, Judge Laguio inhibits himself to preserve their peace of mind. The case is re-raffled to Branch 53, presided by Judge Angel V. Colet, but handled by Pairing Judge Manuel T. Muro.
**May 15, 2000 – June 5, 2000:** Judge Muro grants Yu Yuk Lai's motion for medical confinement at Manila Doctors Hospital for 7 days (overriding the Manila City Jail physician's recommendation for PGH confinement), and later extends it for 1 month or until discharged.
**July 6, 2000 – July 7, 2000:** Judge Muro grants Yu Yuk Lai leave to file a Demurrer to Evidence. Simultaneously, an anonymous letter from "Concerned Court Employees" surfaces alleging Judge Muro's daughter is brokering a multimillion-peso dismissal.
**July 14, 2000:** SP Formaran III files a Motion for Inhibition against Judge Muro, praying he desist from resolving the demurrer to evidence.
**July 16, 2000:** At 7:30 AM, Yu Yuk Lai—supposedly confined at Manila Doctors Hospital—is arrested unescorted while playing baccarat inside the VIP room of Casino Filipino at Holiday Inn Pavilion, Manila.
**July 18, 2000 (Morning):** Hearing on the Motion for Inhibition before Judge Muro concludes and the motion is submitted for resolution. At 11:30 AM, SP Formaran III's secretary informs him that CA Justice Demetria's office called requesting an urgent return call; Formaran calls back, but the Justice is out for lunch.
**July 18, 2000 (1:30 PM – 2:00 PM):** Justice Demetria, PATAFA President Go Teng Kok, and Atty. Reinerio Paas (counsel of Go Teng Kok and close friend of Demetria) personally arrive at SP Formaran III's DOJ office. Go Teng Kok passionately begs Formaran to withdraw the Motion to Inhibit Judge Muro, fearing a new judge will convict Yu Yuk Lai. Demetria inquires about the case status, remarks that anchoring inhibition on an anonymous letter is "a bit dangerous," tells Go Teng Kok to "keep his cool," and expressly asks Formaran if he could "do something to help Go Teng Kok." To terminate the conversation, Formaran states he will consult CSP Jovencito Zuño. Demetria replies **"Iyon pala,"** and leaves. Formaran immediately briefs CSP Zuño and ACSP Guiyab, who both adamantly reject the plea (**"No way!"**).
**July 18, 2000 (Around 3:00 PM):** CSP Zuño receives a direct telephone call from Justice Demetria, who explicitly asks: **"Pakisabi mo nga kay State Prosecutor Formaran na iwithdraw na iyong kanyang Motion to Inhibit para naman makagawa na ng Order si Judge Muro."** CSP Zuño evasively replies that he will see what he can do.
**July 19, 2000 – July 20, 2000:** Judge Muro executes an Order inhibiting himself from the case. Concurrently, national media reports emerge that an appellate magistrate exerted undue pressure on the DOJ to go slow on Yu Yuk Lai. Zuño and Formaran subsequently disclose Justice Demetria's name to clear innocent Supreme Court justices.
**July 21, 2000:** Chief Justice Hilario G. Davide, Jr. issues a Memorandum ordering Justice Demetria to comment on the derogatory news reports.
**August 8, 2000:** The Supreme Court En Banc formally directs an administrative investigation, designating retired Justice Carolina C. Griño-Aquino as Investigator and Court Administrator Alfredo L. Benipayo as Prosecutor.
**January 5, 2001:** Investigating Justice Griño-Aquino submits her formal Report finding Justice Demetria guilty of violating Rule 2.04, Canon 2 of the Code of Judicial Conduct and recommending disciplinary sanction.
### 4. Exhaustive Party Arguments Matrix
A. Respondent Justice Demetrio G. Demetria's Contentions
**Main Thesis:** Respondent never interceded on behalf of Yu Yuk Lai; his presence at the DOJ was purely accidental, his remarks to SP Formaran III were benign and lawful, and he never placed the alleged phone call to CSP Zuño.
**Specific Contentions:**
1.  **Accidental Meeting & Lawful Purpose:** He went to the DOJ merely to visit old friends and see Secretary Artemio Tuquero to assist his close friend Atty. Paas regarding a possible Court of Appeals appointment; his meeting with Go Teng Kok was a spontaneous coincidence.
2.  **Absence of Personal Interest/Acquaintance:** He did not personally know the accused Yu Yuk Lai, Go Teng Kok, or SP Formaran III prior to that day; it is completely illogical and inconceivable for a magistrate to intercede on behalf of total strangers.
3.  **Harmless Inquiries & Pacification:** His statements during the meeting were limited to inquiring about the case status (demonstrating his total lack of prior knowledge), cautioning that anonymous letters are weak grounds for inhibition, and telling Go Teng Kok to "cool it."
4.  **Ambiguity of "Help":** Asking Formaran to "help" Go Teng Kok did not specifically demand the withdrawal of the motion; the requested help was presumed to be "within legal bounds or line of duty."
5.  **Hearsay and Misidentification:** CSP Zuño’s identification of him was inadmissible hearsay based on news accounts and staff statements. In truth, it was Atty. Paas who telephoned CSP Zuño to inquire about the status of the motion.
B. Prosecution / Reporting Witnesses' Contentions (CSP Zuño & SP Formaran III)
**Main Thesis:** Justice Demetria deliberately utilized his official stature, former DOJ rank, and moral ascendancy to exert improper pressure on active prosecutors to withdraw an inhibition motion in an ongoing, non-bailable drug prosecution.
**Specific Contentions:**
1.  **Pre-arranged Coordinated Pressure:** The visit was not accidental. Justice Demetria's office initiated phone calls to Formaran earlier that morning, and Demetria arrived in company with Go Teng Kok and Atty. Paas specifically to corner Formaran.
2.  **Contextualized Plea for Help:** The request to "do something to help Go Teng Kok" occurred while Go Teng Kok was pleading for the withdrawal of the motion to inhibit Judge Muro; in context, no other "help" was contemplated.
3.  **Direct Telephone Intercession:** Justice Demetria directly called CSP Zuño at 3:00 PM, utilizing his moral ascendancy as a former DOJ Undersecretary/Acting Secretary and sitting CA Justice, verbatim instructing Zuño to tell Formaran to withdraw the motion so Judge Muro could issue his order.
4.  **Gross Ethical Breach:** Under Rule 2.04 of the Code of Judicial Conduct, any interference by a magistrate in a matter pending before another court or agency completely erodes public confidence in the judicial branch.
### 5. Complete Inventory of Issues
1.  **[PRIMARY SYLLABUS ISSUE]** Whether or not Court of Appeals Associate Justice Demetrio G. Demetria committed gross misconduct by improperly interfering in a criminal proceeding pending before a trial court and the Department of Justice in violation of Rule 2.04, Canon 2 of the Code of Judicial Conduct, warranting the exercise of the Supreme Court's constitutional disciplinary power to dismiss him from the service.
### 6. Deep-Dive Verdict & Ratio Decidendi
(a) Issue & Short Answer
**Whether or not Justice Demetria violated Rule 2.04, Canon 2 of the Code of Judicial Conduct by attempting to intercede on behalf of an accused in a pending criminal case, thereby justifying his dismissal from the judiciary.**
**YES.** Respondent Justice Demetria actively and improperly used the prestige and moral ascendancy of his judicial office to influence active prosecutors to withdraw a Motion for Inhibition in a high-profile drug trafficking case, violating the fundamental ethical mandate prohibiting judicial interference.
(b) Step-by-Step Ratio Decidendi
1.  **Credibility of Positive Assertion over Bare Denial:** The Supreme Court accepted the positive, detailed, and consistent testimonies of CSP Zuño and SP Formaran III over Justice Demetria's unsubstantiated negative denials. Formaran's statement that Demetria asked him to "help" Go Teng Kok, followed by Zuño's receipt of Demetria's explicit phone call, fully accorded with the natural course of human events and the sequential flow of their encounter.
2.  **The Pretextual Nature of the "Accidental Visit" Defense:** Demetria's defense of an accidental social visit was thoroughly shattered by his own witnesses:
In his initial formal Compliance to the Chief Justice, Demetria claimed he dropped by Formaran's room because Formaran was "also a friend"—yet on the witness stand, Demetria admitted he had never met Formaran or his room partner before.
Witnesses ACSP Gaña and SSP Dañosos confirmed Demetria did not meaningfully visit them (Gaña testified Demetria merely waved "hi," while Dañosos testified he never saw Demetria at all).
The Court found that the timing of the morning call from Demetria's chamber, followed by his afternoon arrival with Go Teng Kok and Atty. Paas directly at the office of the prosecutor handling Yu Yuk Lai's case, could not have been coincidence, but was a coordinated, pre-arranged deployment of judicial influence.
3.  **The True Character of the Requested "Help":** While Demetria argued that asking Formaran to "help" Go Teng Kok could have meant lawful assistance, the Court evaluated the statement within its immediate factual context. Go Teng Kok was at that exact moment vehemently demanding the withdrawal of the motion to inhibit Judge Muro. Demetria's prompt, reinforcing request to "do something to help Go Teng Kok" was a clear judicial endorsement of that illicit demand.
4.  **Moral Ascendancy and the Direct Zuño Telephone Call:** The defense claim that Atty. Paas made the 3:00 PM call to CSP Zuño was rejected as an absurd strain on credulity. CSP Zuño knew Demetria well as his former departmental superior (DOJ Undersecretary and Acting Secretary). Demetria was the only person possessing the stature and moral ascendancy to issue the authoritative command: **"Pakisabi mo nga kay State Prosecutor Formaran na iwithdraw na iyong kanyang Motion to Inhibit para naman makagawa na ng Order si Judge Muro."**
5.  **Absence of Prior Personal Acquaintance Irrelevant:** The Court held that Demetria did not need to personally know Yu Yuk Lai or SP Formaran III to commit the offense. It was sufficient that he was an intimate friend of Atty. Paas (counsel to Yu Yuk Lai's champion, Go Teng Kok), and willingly deployed his high office to exert improper leverage on behalf of that network.
6.  **Absolute Prohibition against Interference:** The Court underscored that Rule 2.04 strictly prohibits a judge from influencing **in any manner** litigation pending before another court or agency. The slightest interference degrades the independence, impartiality, and integrity of the entire judicial system. By engaging in brazen backchannel advocacy for a suspected drug queen, Demetria caused incalculable institutional damage, proving himself unfit to occupy a seat in the Judiciary.
(c) Golden Verbatim Quotes
"The Code of Judicial Conduct mandates a judge to 'refrain from influencing in any manner the outcome of litigation or dispute pending before another court or administrative agency.' The slightest form of interference cannot be countenanced. Once a judge uses his influence to derail or interfere in the regular course of a legal or judicial proceeding for the benefit of one or any of the parties therein, public confidence in the judicial system is diminished, if not totally eroded." (407 Phil. at 674)
"Although every office in the government service is a public trust, no position exacts a greater demand on moral righteousness and uprightness than a seat in the Judiciary. High ethical principles and a sense of propriety should be maintained, without which the faith of the people in the Judiciary so indispensable in an orderly society cannot be preserved. There is simply no place in the Judiciary for those who cannot meet the exacting standards of judicial conduct and integrity." (407 Phil. at 679)
(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation
Even if an appellate justice does not personally know the criminal defendant, accompanying a lobbyist into a trial prosecutor's office and personally telephoning the Chief State Prosecutor to demand the withdrawal of a motion to inhibit a friendly trial judge constitutes gross interference. Under Rule 2.04 of the Code of Judicial Conduct, any attempt by a magistrate to leverage their official prestige or moral ascendancy over pending proceedings before another court or agency severely erodes public faith in the administration of justice and warrants immediate dismissal from the bench with forfeiture of all benefits.
### 6.5. Subject-Specific Doctrinal & Recitation Spotlight
**Assigned Course & Syllabus Focus:** Constitutional Law I → Article VIII: The Judicial Department → Disciplinary Power over Lower-court Justices and Judges.
**State Power vs. Constitutional Limitation:**
 State Power Exercised:** Supreme Court's plenary constitutional disciplinary authority over lower court judges and justices under Article VIII, Section 11 of the 1987 Constitution, enforced through **sua sponte administrative proceedings under its administrative supervision power (Article VIII, Section 6).
 Constitutional / Ethical Standard Applied: The constitutional mandate of "good behavior" during tenure (Art. VIII, Sec. 11), interpreted through the ethical mandates of the Code of Judicial Conduct (Rule 2.04).
**Doctrinal Requisites Checklist (Rule 2.04 Judicial Interference):**
1.  **Actor is a Sitting Magistrate:** Met. Respondent was an Associate Justice of the Court of Appeals.
2.  **Pending Litigation/Dispute:** Met. Criminal drug prosecution pending before RTC Manila, Branch 53 (Judge Muro), with active prosecutorial incidents before the DOJ Task Force.
3.  **Act of Influence "in Any Manner":** Met. Personal appearance at the prosecutor's office advocating for the lobbyist, followed by an explicit phone directive to the Chief State Prosecutor to pull a motion to inhibit.
4.  **Derailment/Prejudice to Impartial Justice:** Met. The act sought to clear the path for a favored pairing judge to grant a demurrer to evidence for a non-bailable drug trafficker caught gambling in casinos.
**Subject-Specific Terms of Art ("Magic Words"):**
 Moral Ascendancy: The authoritative leverage exerted by Demetria as a former DOJ Undersecretary and sitting appellate judge over active state prosecutors.
 Good Behavior: The constitutional condition precedent under Article VIII, Section 11 for judicial tenure, forfeited upon engaging in corrupt intercession.
 Appearance of Impropriety: The standard requiring judges to avoid not merely actual corruption, but any conduct suggesting backchannel influence.
**Cold-Call Synthesis (The 30-Second Recit Answer):**
**In Re: Demetria** exemplifies the Supreme Court En Banc's constitutional power under Article VIII, Section 11 to dismiss an appellate justice for failing the standard of "good behavior." Justice Demetria violated Rule 2.04 of the Code of Judicial Conduct by using his moral ascendancy as a Court of Appeals Justice and former DOJ Undersecretary to lobby prosecutors to withdraw an inhibition motion against a trial judge in a major drug trafficking case. The Court established that judicial interference "in any manner" with cases pending before other courts or agencies causes irreparable institutional damage, leaving zero tolerance for the offender in the Judiciary.
### 7. Separate Opinions & Overall Verdict (Fallo)
**Separate Opinions Summary:** No separate opinions filed. The decision was unanimous (**Per Curiam**), with fourteen (14) Justices concurring and one (1) Justice on official business abroad.
**Verbatim Fallo:**
"WHEREFORE, we sustain the findings of the Investigating Justice and hold Justice Demetrio G. Demetria GUILTY of violating Rule 2.04 of the Code of Judicial Conduct. He is ordered DISMISSED from the service with forfeiture of all benefits and with prejudice to his appointment or reappointment to any government office, agency or instrumentality, including any government owned or controlled corporation or institution.
SO ORDERED."
**Plain-Language Outcome:** Court of Appeals Associate Justice Demetrio G. Demetria was found guilty of gross judicial misconduct, stripped of his judicial office, dismissed from the service, stripped of all retirement and accrued benefits, and permanently barred from holding any public office in the Philippine government.

### 1. Case Header, Cast of Characters & Procedural Posture
**Concise Recognizable Title: In Re: Letter of Presiding Justice Vasquez (CA-G.R. SP No. 103692 / Meralco-GSIS Dispute)**
**Full Official Caption:** Re: Letter of Presiding Justice Conrado M. Vasquez, Jr. on CA-G.R. SP No. 103692 [Antonio Rosete, et al. v. Securities and Exchange Commission, et al.]
**Citation & Metadata:** A.M. No. 08-8-11-CA; 586 Phil. 321; Promulgated September 9, 2008; **Per Curiam**; En Banc. Puno, C.J., Quisumbing, Ynares-Santiago, Carpio, Austria-Martinez, Corona, Carpio-Morales, Azcuna, Tinga, Chico-Nazario, Velasco, Jr., Nachura, Reyes, Leonardo-De Castro, and Brion, JJ., concurring. Two Justices were permitted to inhibit; offers of three other Justices to recuse were denied.
**Voting Breakdown on Penalties:**
**Justice Vicente Q. Roxas:** 12 Justices voted for Dismissal from service; 1 voted for 6 months suspension.
**Justice Jose L. Sabio, Jr.:** 10 Justices voted for 2 months suspension without pay; 1 voted for 6 months suspension; 1 voted for reprimand (as a whistleblower); 1 voted for dismissal.
**Justice Bienvenido L. Reyes:** 8 Justices voted for Reprimand; 5 voted for 1 month suspension.
**Presiding Justice Conrado M. Vasquez, Jr. & Justice Myrna Dimaranan-Vidal:** Unanimous voting (Severe Reprimand and Admonition, respectively).
**Key Parties & Roles (The Cast):**
**Presiding Justice Conrado M. Vasquez, Jr. (PJ Vasquez):** Presiding Justice, Court of Appeals (CA); referred the controversy to the Supreme Court after an emergency CA En Banc session.
**Associate Justice Vicente Q. Roxas (Justice Roxas):** CA Associate Justice; **ponente** in CA-G.R. SP No. 103692.
**Associate Justice Jose L. Sabio, Jr. (Justice Sabio):** CA Associate Justice; designated Acting Chairman of the Special Ninth Division in place of an inhibiting senior member.
**Associate Justice Bienvenido L. Reyes (Justice Reyes):** CA Associate Justice; regular Chairman of the Ninth Division who went on leave and later contested the chairmanship of the case upon return.
**Associate Justice Myrna Dimaranan-Vidal (Justice Dimaranan-Vidal):** CA Associate Justice; member of the Special Ninth Division who signed the initial TRO and a draft decision.
**Associate Justice Apolinario D. Bruselas, Jr. (Justice Bruselas):** CA Associate Justice; junior member of the Eighth Division following the July 4, 2008 CA reorganization.
**Associate Justice Edgardo P. Cruz (Justice Cruz):** CA Associate Justice; Chairman of the CA Rules Committee consulted by Justice Reyes and PJ Vasquez.
**Associate Justice Martin S. Villarama, Jr. (Justice Villarama):** CA Associate Justice; consulted informally by various justices regarding the interpretation of the Internal Rules of the Court of Appeals (IRCA).
**Chairman Camilo L. Sabio (Chairman Sabio):** Chairman, Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG); older brother of Justice Sabio who phoned him regarding the case.
**Francis R. De Borja (Mr. De Borja):** Businessman/broker who met with Justice Sabio at the Ateneo Law School regarding the Meralco dispute.
**Antonio V. Rosete, Manuel M. Lopez, et al. (Meralco):** Petitioners in CA-G.R. SP No. 103692.
**Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) & Government Service Insurance System (GSIS):** Public and corporate respondents in CA-G.R. SP No. 103692; GSIS represented by Chief Legal Counsel Atty. Estrella C. Elamparo.
**Panel of Investigators:** Constituted by the Supreme Court on August 4, 2008, composed of retired Supreme Court Justices Carolina Griño-Aquino (Chairperson), Flerida Ruth P. Romero (Member), and Romeo J. Callejo, Sr. (Member).
**How the Case Reached the Supreme Court:** Administrative referral by letter dated August 1, 2008, from CA Presiding Justice Conrado M. Vasquez, Jr., submitting to the Supreme Court for appropriate action the public dispute, irregularities, and allegations of bribery, impropriety, and rule infractions among appellate court justices relative to CA-G.R. SP No. 103692 (**Antonio Rosete, et al. v. SEC, et al.**), pursuant to the resolution adopted at the CA Emergency En Banc Session of July 31, 2008.
### 2. Syllabus Topic Grouping, Codal Provision & Factual Trigger
**Primary Topic Hierarchy:** Constitutional Law I → Judicial Department → Disciplinary Power over Lower-Court Justices and Judges (Art. VIII, Sec. 6 and Sec. 11, 1987 Constitution).
**Secondary Topic Hierarchy:** Legal & Judicial Ethics → Code of Judicial Conduct & Canons of Professional Responsibility → Gross Misconduct, Gross Inefficiency, Dishonesty, and Conduct Unbecoming a Member of the Judiciary.
**Full Text of Governing Constitutional / Statutory Provisions:**
**Article VIII, Section 6, 1987 Constitution:**
"The Supreme Court shall have **administrative supervision over all courts and the personnel thereof**."
**Article VIII, Section 11, 1987 Constitution:**
"The Members of the Supreme Court and judges of lower courts shall hold office during good behavior until they reach the age of seventy years or become incapacitated to discharge the duties of their office. **The Supreme Court en banc shall have the power to discipline judges of lower courts, or order their dismissal by a vote of a majority of the Members who actually took part in the deliberations on the issues in the case and voted thereon**."
**Factual Trigger (Application to the Story):** The controversy erupted when a high-stakes corporate control dispute between Meralco management and the GSIS/SEC was brought before the Court of Appeals via CA-G.R. SP No. 103692. The assigned **ponente**, Justice Roxas, issued a Temporary Restraining Order (TRO) with an acting division chair, Justice Sabio, but ignored multiple prejudicial and urgent motions, including a motion for his own inhibition and a motion to lift the TRO. When the regular division chair, Justice Reyes, returned from leave, an acrimonious battle over the division chairmanship ensued, exacerbated by an outside call from PCGG Chairman Camilo Sabio attempting to influence his brother Justice Sabio, and an alleged ₱10-million bribe offer by businessman Francis De Borja to induce Justice Sabio to yield the chairmanship to Justice Reyes. Amidst deliberate fabrications of deliberation transcripts, the sudden discarding of a signed draft decision, and open disregard of the Presiding Justice’s pending resolution of an "interpleader," Justices Roxas, Reyes, and Bruselas hastily promulgated a final decision on the merits, causing the scandal to explode into public media and precipitating an emergency En Banc referral to the Supreme Court.
### 3. Chronological Facts Storyboard
**April 15, 2008:** Justice Reyes, regular Chairman of the CA Ninth Division, files an application for leave of absence from May 15 to June 5, 2008.
**May 14, 2008:** Presiding Justice Vasquez issues Office Order No. 149-08-CMV designating Justice Jose C. Mendoza as Acting Chairman of the Ninth Division during Justice Reyes's leave to act on all cases submitted for final resolution and/or appropriate action, except **ponencia**.
**May 29, 2008 (10:48 AM – 10:49 AM):** Meralco officers and directors file a Petition for **Certiorari** and Prohibition with urgent prayer for TRO and preliminary injunction against the SEC and GSIS, docketed as CA-G.R. SP No. 103692. Meralco simultaneously files an urgent motion for special raffle, which PJ Vasquez approves via a handwritten marginal note. The case is raffled to Justice Roxas.
**May 29, 2008 (3:10 PM – 4:10 PM):** GSIS Chief Legal Counsel Atty. Estrella C. Elamparo requests a re-raffle of the case in the presence of the parties and files an **Ex-Parte** Motion to Defer Action on any incident pending resolution of the re-raffle request. GSIS lawyers attempt to serve the motion personally at Justice Roxas's chambers, but staff decline to sign or acknowledge receipt.
**May 30, 2008 (Morning):** Justice Reyes files an extension of his leave to June 6, 2008. Justice Mendoza formally inhibits from CA-G.R. SP No. 103692 because he was a former Meralco legal counsel. Justice Roxas files an "Emergency Request for Raffle," and Justice Jose L. Sabio, Jr. is selected as Acting Chairman of the Special Ninth Division vice Justice Mendoza. Justice Roxas sends an emergency deliberation notice to Justice Dimaranan-Vidal, citing "national interest." Atty. Elamparo receives an anonymous call alleging a TRO is already drafted and that Meralco lawyers are in direct contact with Justice Roxas.
**May 30, 2008 (11:58 AM):** GSIS files an Urgent **Ex-Parte** Motion to Inhibit Justice Roxas based on reports of premature TRO preparation and pending administrative charges against him.
**May 30, 2008 (1:30 PM):** PCGG Chairman Camilo Sabio calls his brother, Justice Sabio, urging him to help GSIS and the SEC as representatives of the public interest against Meralco. Justice Sabio responds that he will vote according to his conscience and schedule the injunctive relief for oral arguments.
**May 30, 2008 (2:08 PM – 4:03 PM):** Justice Roxas brings a pre-drafted TRO to Justice Sabio's chambers, already signed by Roxas and Justice Dimaranan-Vidal. Justice Sabio signs upon the condition that hearings be set for June 23 and 24, 2008. The Special Ninth Division issues the TRO and directs comments within 10 days. Justice Roxas considers the issuance of the TRO an "implied denial" of the GSIS motion to inhibit him, leaving it unacted upon in writing. At 3:00 PM, GSIS files an Urgent Motion to Lift the TRO; Justice Roxas takes no formal action.
**May 31, 2008:** Businessman Francis De Borja calls Justice Sabio, congratulating him with **"Mabuhay ka, Justice,"** stating the Makati Business Club is pleased with the TRO. Justice Sabio replies that he voted according to his conscience.
**June 10, 2008:** Regular Chairman Justice Reyes reports back to duty at the Court of Appeals.
**June 16, 2008:** CA Division Clerk of Court Atty. Teresita Custodio delivers the **cartilla** (case brief) of CA-G.R. SP No. 103692 to Justice Reyes. Hours later, Atty. Custodio retrieves it under instruction from Justice Sabio, who insists he retains authority over the case. Justice Reyes feels affronted and examines the IRCA rules.
**June 17–19, 2008:** Justice Reyes consults PJ Vasquez regarding the conflict. On June 19, 2008, Justice Reyes formally writes PJ Vasquez, posing the dilemma of whether the case remains with Justice Sabio's Special Ninth Division under Section 2(d), Rule VI of the IRCA, or reverts to the regular Ninth Division under Justice Reyes.
**June 20, 2008:** PJ Vasquez refers the inquiry to Justice Edgardo P. Cruz, Chairman of the Rules Committee. Justice Cruz renders a written opinion stating that under Section 2(d), Rule VI of the IRCA, the issuance of a TRO is not among the four instances where participating justices remain with a case; thus, the case reverted to regular Chairman Justice Reyes. PJ Vasquez conveys this to Justice Sabio, who angrily rejects Cruz's opinion, claiming Cruz signed in a personal capacity and was junior to him, adding that he "smelled something fishy."
**June 23, 2008:** Before the hearing, Justices Sabio, Roxas, and Reyes separately consult Justice Villarama. Villarama advises Roxas to resolve the motion to lift the TRO and inhibit himself (**"mag-inhibit ka baka magka-problema"**), but Roxas ignores the advice. At the hearing room, Justice Reyes's nameplate is displayed, but Justice Sabio moves the hearing to another room to preside over the Special Ninth Division with Justices Roxas and Dimaranan-Vidal. Justice Reyes refrains from presiding to avoid an "ugly spectacle." Parties agree to submit simultaneous memoranda within 15 days on the injunctive prayer. Justice Roxas does not ask a single question, and the motion for his inhibition is never raised.
**June 25, 2008:** PJ Vasquez issues Office Order No. 200-08-CMV reorganizing the CA effective July 4, 2008: Justice Sabio is designated Chairman of the Sixth Division; Justice Reyes becomes Chairman of the Eighth Division, with Justices Roxas and Bruselas as members.
**July 1, 2008 (Evening):** Francis De Borja meets Justice Sabio at the Ateneo Law School lobby-lounge after Sabio's Legal Ethics class. De Borja mentions being with Manolo Lopez and offers a "win-win situation" consisting of ₱10 million for Justice Sabio to yield the division chairmanship to Justice Reyes, noting Meralco is "more comfortable" with Reyes. Justice Sabio rejects the offer, citing his conscience, family, and ethics professorship. De Borja carries a paper bag during the encounter.
**July 2–3, 2008:** Justice Sabio verbally informs PJ Vasquez and Justice Villarama that he was offered an illicit ₱10-million bribe to step down from the case, but withholds the briber's name. PJ Vasquez takes no formal action, viewing it as a personal matter for Sabio. On July 3, Justice Sabio calls De Borja back to warn him against pestering him.
**July 4, 2008:** CA reorganization takes effect. Justice Reyes visits PJ Vasquez concerning Meralco's urgent moves to have him assume the chairmanship.
**July 8, 2008:** Justice Roxas personally brings a 56-page signed final decision on the merits to Justice Dimaranan-Vidal, urging her to sign immediately due to the approaching expiration of the TRO, despite knowing the parties' memoranda deadlines have not lapsed and not all memoranda are in. Justice Dimaranan-Vidal signs the decision and three extra signature pages.
**July 10, 2008:** Meralco files an Urgent Motion praying that Justice Reyes assume the chairmanship of the Division, arguing that under Section 3(d), Rule IV of the IRCA, a TRO does not retain jurisdiction.
**July 14, 2008:** Justice Roxas bypasses Justice Sabio and Dimaranan-Vidal, bringing the **rollo** directly to Justice Reyes in the Eighth Division. Justices Reyes, Roxas, and Bruselas hold a 10-minute "deliberation." Roxas subsequently constructs a fabricated "Transcript of Final Deliberation" purely from memory—without stenographer, notes, or audio recording—falsely documenting a comprehensive discussion and referring to a non-existent separate "Final Report."
**July 15–17, 2008:** Justice Sabio confronts Justice Reyes in his chambers, accusing him of being a "Trojan horse" and disclosing that he had been offered ₱10 million to step aside for Reyes. Justice Reyes disclaims any corrupt interest, maintaining he only fears administrative charges for nonfeasance.
**July 21, 2008:** Justice Roxas files an "Interpleader Petition" with PJ Vasquez, asking him to decide which Division Chairman (Sabio or Reyes) has lawful authority to act. PJ Vasquez states he will study the matter. Roxas simultaneously endorses the finalized decision to Justice Reyes for signature.
**July 22, 2008:** Justice Reyes writes PJ Vasquez urging him to resolve the chairmanship question immediately, stating that otherwise, he will act according to his best lights.
**July 23, 2008 (12:00 PM – 4:10 PM):** Without awaiting PJ Vasquez's resolution of the Interpleader, Justice Reyes signs the decision and the constitutional certification. Justice Roxas precipitously promulgates the decision on the merits of CA-G.R. SP No. 103692 at 4:10 PM, holding for Meralco and recommending sanctions against GSIS lawyers. The draft decision signed by Justice Dimaranan-Vidal is discarded and shredded/burned by Roxas without informing her.
**July 24, 2008:** PJ Vasquez issues his written opinion concluding that the Special Ninth Division (chaired by Sabio, with Roxas and Vidal) should retain and resolve the injunctive prayer and pending motions. Minutes later, PJ Vasquez learns the decision was already promulgated the afternoon before by the Eighth Division. Justice Dimaranan-Vidal and Justice Bruselas discover the irregular maneuverings, prompting written protests.
**July 31, 2008:** The CA holds an Emergency En Banc Session behind closed doors. The CA En Banc resolves to: (1) refer the propriety of the actions of the justices to the Supreme Court; (2) leave the validity of the decision to the parties in the regular course; and (3) refer IRCA conflicts to the Rules Committee. De Borja executes a public counter-affidavit accusing Justice Sabio of soliciting ₱50 million to resist government pressure. Justice Sabio requests and obtains permission from PJ Vasquez to hold a media press conference.
**August 1, 2008:** PJ Vasquez formally transmits the matter to Chief Justice Reynato S. Puno via letter. Justice Sabio conducts a full public press conference releasing his side of the bribery scandal.
**August 4, 2008:** The Supreme Court creates a three-member Panel of Investigators (retired SC Justices Griño-Aquino, Romero, and Callejo, Sr.).
**September 4, 2008:** The Investigating Panel submits its final report and recommendations finding extensive ethical and statutory violations across all justices involved.
### 4. Exhaustive Party Arguments Matrix
A. Associate Justice Vicente Q. Roxas
**Main Thesis:** The promulgation of the decision by the Eighth Division was legally correct under the IRCA; his handling of the case was driven by extreme urgency to prevent the expiration of the TRO, and any omission or procedural lapse was done without corrupt motive.
**Specific Contentions:**
 On Inaction on Motions: The issuance of the TRO on May 30, 2008 operated as an "implied denial" of GSIS's Motion to Inhibit him; there was no legal necessity to issue a separate written resolution. The motion to lift the TRO and procedural motions lacked merit and required no action prior to deciding the case.
 On the Fabricated Deliberation Minutes: The "Transcript of Final Deliberation" dated July 14, 2008 was prepared "from memory" merely to comply with the formal mandate of Section 9, Rule VI of the IRCA that minutes be kept and to lend credence to the Constitutional certification under Article VIII, Section 13.
 On Discarding Justice Dimaranan-Vidal's Signature: The decision shown to Justice Dimaranan-Vidal on July 8, 2008 was a mere "draft" and "unofficial," which she merely asked to read; it was not a final decision. It was thrown into the wastebasket because the July 4, 2008 reorganization mandatorily transferred the case to the Eighth Division.
 On Bypassing the Presiding Justice: He filed the "Interpleader Petition" on July 21, 2008, but promulgated the decision on July 23, 2008 because he believed the Presiding Justice had no authority under the IRCA to resolve division disputes, and the impending July 30, 2008 expiry of the TRO created a pressing judicial duty to act.
B. Associate Justice Jose L. Sabio, Jr.
**Main Thesis:** He maintained rightful custody and chairmanship over CA-G.R. SP No. 103692 because the Special Ninth Division had taken cognizance, issued the TRO, and heard oral arguments; he was an upright magistrate who staunchly resisted corrupt overtures and acted purely as an ethical whistleblower.
**Specific Contentions:**
 On Chairmanship Retention: Under Section 2(d) and Section 7(b), Rule VI of the IRCA, a division that acts on an injunctive prayer and before which a motion for reconsideration/lifting is pending retains jurisdiction. A TRO is the inception of preliminary injunctive relief.
 On the Call from Chairman Camilo Sabio: He did not yield to his brother's entreaty to help GSIS; he explicitly told his brother he would decide strictly according to his conscience and required GSIS to prove its legal standing during open arguments.

### 5. Complete Inventory of Issues
1. **[PRIMARY SYLLABUS ISSUE]** Whether or not the Supreme Court, in the exercise of its constitutional power of administrative supervision and discipline over lower courts and judges, has the authority to sanction appellate court justices for gross misconduct, dishonesty, undue interest, and conduct unbecoming a judicial officer under the Code of Judicial Conduct and the Rules of Court.
2. **[Secondary Issue]** Whether or not Associate Justice Vicente Q. Roxas is administratively liable for gross dishonesty, undue interest, gross inefficiency, and multiple violations of the Code of Judicial Conduct warranting dismissal from the service.
3. **[Secondary Issue]** Whether or not Associate Justice Jose L. Sabio, Jr. is administratively liable for simple misconduct and conduct unbecoming a justice for entertaining inappropriate ex-parte conversations with his brother PCGG Chairman Camilo Sabio and emissary Francis De Borja, and for clinging stubbornly to the division chairmanship.
4. **[Secondary Issue]** Whether or not Associate Justice Bienvenido L. Reyes is administratively liable for simple misconduct for participating in and signing the final decision while his own request for clarification on the chairmanship was still pending resolution before the Presiding Justice.
5. **[Secondary Issue]** Whether or not Associate Justice Myrna Dimaranan-Vidal is administratively liable for conduct unbecoming a justice for allowing herself to be hurried into signing a decision on the merits before the parties' memoranda were submitted and without division deliberations.
6. **[Secondary Issue]** Whether or not Presiding Justice Conrado M. Vasquez, Jr. is administratively liable for failure to act promptly, decisively, and effectively to manage internal turmoil and preserve the integrity of the Court of Appeals under the IRCA.
7. **[Secondary Issue]** Whether or not PCGG Chairman Camilo L. Sabio and private businessman Francis R. De Borja are subject to disciplinary referral and criminal prosecution, respectively, arising from the factual findings of the Investigating Panel.
### 6. Deep-Dive Verdict & Ratio Decidendi per Issue
Issue 1: Constitutional Disciplinary Authority of the Supreme Court over CA Justices
**(a) Issue & Short Answer:** Does the Supreme Court have the constitutional disciplinary authority to investigate, sanction, and dismiss appellate court justices for ethical and procedural violations? **YES.** The Constitution vests the Supreme Court with plenary administrative supervision over all lower courts and their personnel, including the absolute power to discipline and dismiss judges of lower courts.
**(b) Step-by-Step Ratio Decidendi:**
 Constitutional Anchorage: Under Article VIII, Section 6 and Section 11 of the 1987 Constitution, the Supreme Court En Banc possesses exclusive disciplinary jurisdiction over members of lower courts. Court of Appeals justices are magistrates of an inferior statutory court and fall squarely within this constitutional umbrella.
 Duty of Integrity and Public Confidence: The Judiciary is the firmest pillar of democratic institutions. For decisions to command credibility and legitimacy as part of the law of the land, courts must not only be impartial and independent in fact, but must also be perceived as such by the public.
 Enforceability of Canons: The Code of Judicial Conduct, the New Code of Judicial Conduct for the Philippine Judiciary, Rule 140 of the Rules of Court, and the Civil Service Rules establish binding legal baselines. The Court has the inescapable constitutional duty to cleanse the ranks of the appellate bench when internal conduct fails to conform to the highest standards of decorum and propriety.
**(c) Golden Verbatim Quote:**
"The Judiciary, which is acclaimed as the firmest pillar of our democratic institutions, is vested by the Constitution with the power to settle disputes between parties and to determine their rights and obligations under the law... It is this Court's bounden duty to determine the culpability or innocence of the members of the Judiciary involved in the said controversy and to discipline any one whose conduct has failed to conform to the canons of judicial ethics, which uphold integrity, independence, impartiality, competence and propriety in the performance of official functions."
**(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation:** Under Article VIII, Sections 6 and 11, the Supreme Court En Banc has full constitutional authority to supervise, discipline, and dismiss any lower court judge or appellate justice. When Court of Appeals justices become embroiled in unethical infighting, dishonesty, or corrupt schemes, the Supreme Court acts as the ultimate disciplinary authority to preserve the integrity of the judicial branch.
Issue 2: Administrative Liability of Associate Justice Vicente Q. Roxas
**(a) Issue & Short Answer:** Is Justice Vicente Q. Roxas guilty of multiple violations of the Code of Judicial Conduct, gross misconduct, gross dishonesty, and undue interest warranting dismissal? **YES.** His failure to act on critical motions, deliberate fabrication of deliberation minutes, premature drafting of a decision before receipt of memoranda, and callous discarding of a colleague's signed decision establish gross dishonesty and intolerable bias.
**(b) Step-by-Step Ratio Decidendi:**
 Failure to Act on Motions (Gross Inefficiency):** Justice Roxas deliberately ignored GSIS's Motion to Inhibit him, the Motion to Lift the TRO, and motions regarding presentation aids. His theory that issuing the TRO constituted an "implied denial" of his inhibition is untenable; Section 3, Rule V of the IRCA explicitly mandates that a justice must resolve a motion for inhibition **alone and in writing**. Failing to resolve pending incidents within reglementary periods constitutes gross inefficiency and grave misconduct. Roxas had already been fined ₱15,000 for similar inaction in **Orocio v. Roxas (A.M. Nos. 07-115-CA-J and CA-08-46-J) and warned.
 Gross Dishonesty and Falsification:** Roxas admitted that the "Transcript of Final Deliberation" dated July 14, 2008 was a complete "fabrication" composed purely "from memory" without a stenographer, notes, or audio recording. It falsely asserted that division members had held "previous deliberations" and reviewed a "Final Report" of the **ponente, when in truth, no prior deliberations occurred and the supposed "Report" was merely the pre-signed decision itself.
 Deceit Regarding Justice Vidal: Roxas lied under oath to the Panel by claiming he brought the decision to Justice Dimaranan-Vidal on July 8 merely as an informal "draft" for reading. Vidal established that Roxas brought it for formal signature, obtained her concurrence and three signature pages, and subsequently shredded/burned her signed copy without notice when he decided to execute a forum-shift to the Eighth Division.
 Manifest Undue Interest and Unseemly Haste: Roxas began drafting and completing the 56-page decision on the merits before the July 8, 2008 deadline for the parties' memoranda had expired, rendering the substantial work of counsel futile. He rushed to judgment, bypassed the pending Interpleader he himself submitted to PJ Vasquez on July 21, and promulgated the ruling on July 23 without waiting for the Presiding Justice's opinion. Such conduct exhibits a desperate and unseemly rush to judgment favoring Meralco.
**(c) Golden Verbatim Quote:**
"The so-called 'transcript' is a fabrication designed to deceive that there had been compliance - when actually there was none - with the prerequisite of the IRCA that consultation and/or deliberation among the members of the Division must precede the drafting of a decision... Dishonesty, being in the nature of a grave offense, carries the extreme penalty of dismissal from the service with forfeiture of retirement benefits except accrued leave credits, and perpetual disqualification for re-employment in the government service. Dishonesty has no place in the judiciary."
**(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation:** Justice Roxas committed multiple capital judicial offenses: he fabricated deliberation records from memory, drafted a final decision before the parties even filed their legal memoranda, lied about showing a colleague a mere "draft" when he had actually obtained her formal signature, shredded her signed copy, and ignored mandatory rules requiring written orders on motions for his inhibition. The Court held that this combination of gross dishonesty and manifest partiality demanded the supreme administrative sanction of dismissal.
Issue 3: Administrative Liability of Associate Justice Jose L. Sabio, Jr.
**(a) Issue & Short Answer:** Is Justice Jose L. Sabio, Jr. guilty of simple misconduct and conduct unbecoming a justice for improper communications and clinging to the chairmanship? **YES.** Entertaining an improper telephone entreaty from his PCGG Chairman brother, meeting privately with a corporate fixer, calling that fixer back after a bribe attempt, and stubbornly holding onto a temporary acting chairmanship warrant a two-month suspension without pay.
**(b) Step-by-Step Ratio Decidendi:**
 Improper Conversation with Chairman Camilo Sabio: Although Justice Sabio signed the TRO and told his brother he would vote according to his conscience, he committed a serious ethical lapse by entertaining his brother's substantive pitch on behalf of GSIS. Under Canon 1, Sections 1, 4, and 5 of the New Code of Judicial Conduct, judges must keep the judicial function free from family influence and inappropriate connections with the Executive branch.
 Indiscreet Meetings and Communications with Francis De Borja: Knowing De Borja was a corporate dealmaker, Justice Sabio exhibited egregious indiscretion by agreeing to meet him privately at the Ateneo Law School lobby to discuss the Meralco case. He broke the shield of judicial confidentiality. While the Court credited Sabio's report that De Borja offered him a ₱10-million bribe (and discredited De Borja's retaliatory claim of a ₱50-million solicitation), Justice Sabio's act of calling De Borja back on July 3, 2008 displayed shocking poor judgment. A magistrate insulted by an attempted bribe should immediately cut off all communication and report the crime, rather than maintain phone contact.
 Clinging to Division Chairmanship: Justice Sabio's designation as Acting Chairman of the Ninth Division was strictly limited to the absence of Justice Reyes. Once Reyes reported back to duty on June 10, 2008, Sabio had no legal right to retain the chair. His refusal to yield, his dismissive attitude toward Justice Cruz's opinion, and his unilateral drafting of resolutions created an unnecessary and scandalous impasse.
**(c) Golden Verbatim Quote:**
"Instead of telling off De Borja that he could not, and would not, talk about the Meralco case, Justice Sabio, Jr. agreed to meet De Borja in the lobby-lounge of the Ateneo Law School after his evening class in Legal Ethics in said school. Justice Sabio Jr.'s action of discussing the Meralco case with De Borja was highly inappropriate and indiscreet... the continued communications between Justice Sabio and Mr. De Borja even after the latter's rejected bribery attempt is highly inappropriate and shows poor judgment on the part of Justice Sabio who should have acted in preservation of the dignity of his judicial office..."
**(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation:** Even though Justice Sabio rejected the ₱10-million bribe and blew the whistle, he committed simple misconduct. He broke judicial confidentiality by discussing an active case with his brother and an outside broker, exercised appalling judgment by calling the bribe-giver back on the phone, and aggressively clung to a temporary acting chairmanship after the regular division chair had already returned from leave.
Issue 4: Administrative Liability of Associate Justice Bienvenido L. Reyes
**(a) Issue & Short Answer:** Is Justice Bienvenido L. Reyes guilty of simple misconduct for signing and promulgating the decision while his formal inquiry to the Presiding Justice remained pending? **YES.** Precipitously signing and promulgating the decision without waiting for the Presiding Justice's ruling on the division impasse constituted discourtesy and simple misconduct, mitigated by his prior efforts to seek guidance.
**(b) Step-by-Step Ratio Decidendi:**
 Breach of Judicial Courtesy and Due Process: Justice Reyes formally requested PJ Vasquez on June 19 and July 22, 2008 to clarify whether his Eighth Division or Sabio's Special Ninth Division held lawful authority over the case. PJ Vasquez had informed him that he was actively reviewing the matter.
 Precipitate Promulgation:** Despite having actively sought the Presiding Justice's ruling, Justice Reyes signed the decision and Article VIII, Section 13 certification at noon on July 23, 2008, enabling Roxas to promulgate it that afternoon. He never withdrew his query nor gave advance warning to PJ Vasquez. When PJ Vasquez issued his ruling on July 24, it was rendered **functus officio, embarrassing and humiliating the head of the court.
 Mitigation: Under Canon 5, Section 3 of the New Code of Judicial Conduct, judges must show professional regard for judicial colleagues. However, the offense is mitigated because Justice Reyes repeatedly consulted the leadership in good faith and was motivated by an apprehension of administrative liability for nonfeasance under the IRCA. Hence, reprimand is the appropriate penalty.
**(c) Golden Verbatim Quote:**
"Thus, when the Presiding Justice issued his ruling on the chairmanship dispute on July 24, 2008, he was unaware of the promulgation of the Meralco decision on July 23, 2008, under the aegis of Justice Reyes' Eighth Division... 'Presiding Justice Vasquez, Jr. was completely taken aback when he learned about it on July 24, 2008, the same day that he issued his opinion on the chairmanship issue which by then had become functus officio. He felt belittled and humiliated by the discourtesy of the two justices to him.'"
**(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation:** Justice Reyes asked Presiding Justice Vasquez to resolve who should chair the division, but then turned around and signed the final decision before the Presiding Justice could even release his opinion. Because he rendered his own chief magistrate's pending resolution completely useless and humiliated him, he was found guilty of simple misconduct, though penalized only with a reprimand due to mitigating good faith.
Issue 5: Administrative Liability of Associate Justice Myrna Dimaranan-Vidal
**(a) Issue & Short Answer:** Is Justice Myrna Dimaranan-Vidal guilty of conduct unbecoming a justice for signing a decision prematurely under pressure from the **ponente**? **YES.** Submitting to the rushed demands of Justice Roxas to sign a 56-page decision without reading the parties' memoranda and without collegiate deliberations exhibited weakness and a lack of judicial independence.
**(b) Step-by-Step Ratio Decidendi:**
 Abdication of Independent Duty: Under Canon 1, Sections 1 and 2 of the New Code of Judicial Conduct, a judge must exercise judicial functions independently, free from pressure from any quarter, including judicial colleagues.
 Procedural Dereliction: Justice Vidal knew that the TRO was not set to expire until July 29/30, 2008—three full weeks away—and that the parties' memoranda deadlines had not elapsed. Despite this, she allowed herself to be hurried by Justice Roxas into signing the decision on July 8 without collegiate deliberations. Yielding to improper practices of colleagues constitutes conduct unbecoming a justice, warranting an admonition.
**(c) Golden Verbatim Quote:**
"Justice Dimaranan-Vidal deviated from the IRCA when she allowed herself to be rushed by Justice Roxas to sign the Meralco decision on July 8, 2008, without reading the parties' memoranda and without the deliberation among members of the Division required by the IRCA. She knew that the TRO would not expire until July 30, 2008 - some three (3) weeks away from July 8, 2008 - yet she allowed herself to believe Justice Roxas' misrepresentation that signing the decision was urgent. Her compliance with certain dissembling practices of other justices of the Court, in violation of the IRCA, showed weakness and lack of independence on her part."
**(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation:** An appellate judge cannot simply rubber-stamp a colleague's decision because she is told it is "urgent." Justice Vidal bowed to Justice Roxas's pressure and signed a complete ruling on the merits three weeks before the TRO expired, before reading the parties' legal briefs, and without holding required division deliberations. She was formally admonished to be more circumspect and independent.
Issue 6: Administrative Liability of Presiding Justice Conrado M. Vasquez, Jr.
**(a) Issue & Short Answer:** Did Presiding Justice Conrado M. Vasquez, Jr. commit administrative lapses warranting sanction for failing to act decisively? **YES.** His indecision, vacillation, and failure to invoke his express emergency powers under the IRCA to halt the division war and investigate the bribery report warrant a severe reprimand.
**(b) Step-by-Step Ratio Decidendi:**
 Failure of Executive Leadership: Under Section 11, Rule VIII of the IRCA, the Presiding Justice is explicitly authorized to act "on any matter not covered by these Rules." Furthermore, Section 5(c), Rule I of the IRCA mandates that the CA En Banc adopt uniform policies to protect and preserve the integrity of judicial processes.
 Paralysis in the Face of Crisis: When Justice Sabio reported a ₱10-million bribe attempt on July 2, 2008, PJ Vasquez failed to convene the Court En Banc or initiate an immediate inquiry, brushing it aside as a personal matter. He temporized on resolving the chairmanship impasse between Sabio and Reyes, passively watching the tensions escalate until the court's institutional integrity was catastrophically damaged.
**(c) Golden Verbatim Quote:**
"Clearly, Presiding Justice Vasquez, Jr. had been indecisive in dealing with the turmoil arising from the Meralco case. He vacillated and temporized on resolving the impasse between Justice Sabio, Jr. and Justice B. L. Reyes over the chairmanship of the Division that should hear and decide the Meralco case. He failed to take action on the reported bribe-offer by Meralco to J. Sabio, Jr... Was he not aware then, or did he discover too late, that under Section 11, Rule VIII of the IRCA, he is in fact authorized to act 'on any matter' involving the Court and its members?"
**(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation:** As head of the Court of Appeals, the Presiding Justice had both the authority and the affirmative duty under the IRCA to step in, resolve procedural stalemates, and convene the En Banc immediately upon hearing that a justice was offered a ₱10-million bribe. Because he hesitated, vacillated, and sat on the sidelines while the scandal spun out of control, the Supreme Court severely reprimanded him.
Issue 7: Liabilities of PCGG Chairman Camilo Sabio and Francis De Borja
**(a) Issue & Short Answer:** Should PCGG Chairman Camilo Sabio and Francis De Borja be referred for disciplinary and criminal investigation? **YES.** Chairman Sabio's attempt to influence his brother violated the legal ethics governing attorneys, warranting referral to the Bar Confidant; Francis De Borja's attempted bribery of a sitting justice warranted criminal referral to the Department of Justice (DOJ).
**(b) Step-by-Step Ratio Decidendi:**
 PCGG Chairman Sabio (Legal Ethics): Under Canon 13 of the Code of Professional Responsibility, a lawyer shall refrain from any impropriety that tends to influence, or gives the appearance of influencing, the court. Chairman Sabio's telephonic intervention requesting his magistrate-brother to "help GSIS" directly violated legal ethics, warranting referral to the Office of the Bar Confidant.
 Francis De Borja (Criminal Liability): The evidence credited by the Panel established that De Borja approached Justice Sabio offering ₱10 million to step down from the case in favor of Justice Reyes. This constitutes attempted bribery of a judicial officer, requiring referral to the DOJ for criminal prosecution.
**(c) Golden Verbatim Quote:**
"With respect to Chairman Sabio, this Court has the power to discipline members of the Bar and his attempt to influence a member of the Judiciary, his brother at that, should be referred to the Bar Confidant for appropriate action. With respect to Mr. De Borja, the present investigation has given this Court reason to believe that Mr. De Borja may be criminally liable for his attempt to bribe a magistrate of the Court of Appeals. This matter should be referred to the Department of Justice for appropriate action."
**(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation:** The Supreme Court's reach extended beyond the justices themselves. The Court referred PCGG Chairman Sabio to the Bar Confidant for disbarment/disciplinary proceedings for trying to sway his brother's judicial vote, and referred Francis De Borja to the DOJ for criminal indictment for attempted bribery.
### 6.5. Subject-Specific Doctrinal & Recitation Spotlight
**Assigned Course & Syllabus Focus:** Constitutional Law I → Judicial Department → Disciplinary Power over Lower-court Justices and Judges (Art. VIII, Sec. 6 & Sec. 11).
**Doctrinal Requisites / Elements Checklist:**
Under Article VIII, Section 11 of the 1987 Constitution and Rule 140 of the Rules of Court:
1.  **Grounds for Dismissal / Severe Sanctions:** Serious misconduct, gross inefficiency, dishonesty, and violations of the Code of Judicial Conduct.
 Applied to Roxas: Gross dishonesty (fabrication of deliberation minutes), gross inefficiency (failure to act on prejudice-inducing motions to inhibit and lift TRO), and undue interest (deciding before memoranda filed) → **Dismissal meted**.
2.  **Grounds for Suspension / Reprimand:** Less serious charges, simple misconduct, and conduct unbecoming a judge.
 Applied to Sabio: Improper private meetings with an emissary, calling back a bribe-giver, violating judicial confidentiality, and refusing to surrender an acting seat → **2 months suspension**.
 Applied to Reyes: Promoting the hasty promulgation of a decision while submitting an active query on the same issue to his chief justice → **Reprimand (mitigated)**.
 Applied to Dimaranan-Vidal: Abdicating independent duty by hastily executing signature pages without reading party submissions or participating in deliberations → **Admonition**.
 Applied to PJ Vasquez: Dereliction of administrative leadership and failure to convene the En Banc to preserve judicial integrity under the IRCA → **Severe Reprimand**.
**Subject-Specific Terms of Art ("Magic Words"):**
 Plenary Administrative Supervision: The constitutional umbrella (Art. VIII, Sec. 6) empowering the Supreme Court to regulate, investigate, and correct lower tribunals.
 Power to Discipline and Dismiss (Art. VIII, Sec. 11): Absolute constitutional authority of the Supreme Court En Banc over inferior court judges.
 Appearance of Impropriety: The standard requiring judges to avoid not just corruption, but even the perception of partiality.
 Functus Officio: Rendering an official act or proceeding moot and stripped of operational vitality.
 Falsification / Gross Dishonesty: Conscious perversion of the truth in official records (such as fabricating division minutes "from memory").
**Cold-Call Synthesis (The 30-Second Recit Answer):**
"**In Re: Letter of PJ Vasquez** is a foundational Constitutional Law I precedent on the Supreme Court's disciplinary power over the Court of Appeals under Article VIII, Sections 6 and 11. Arising from a judicial brawl over the Meralco-GSIS corporate dispute, the Supreme Court exercised its plenary administrative power to sanction five appellate justices simultaneously: dismissing Justice Roxas for gross dishonesty, fabricated deliberation minutes, and unseemly haste; suspending Justice Sabio for two months for improper communications with a corporate fixer and his PCGG brother; reprimanding Justice Reyes for premature promulgation; admonishing Justice Vidal for abdicating independence; and severely reprimanding Presiding Justice Vasquez for indecisive leadership. The case crystallizes that the Supreme Court will enforce the highest ethical standards across the appellate bench to preserve public confidence in the administration of justice."
**Constitutional & Political Law Lens:**
 State Power vs. Constitutional Limitation: The Court exercised its inherent and textual constitutional power of judicial self-cleansing and administrative discipline (Art. VIII, Secs. 6 & 11) over lower court judges who breached the separation of ethical standards and violated the Code of Judicial Conduct.
 Level of Judicial Scrutiny / Doctrinal Test: Substantial evidence standard in administrative proceedings against judges, coupled with the strict application of Rule 140 and the New Code of Judicial Conduct. Dishonesty carries a strict per se dismissal rule upon first commission.
 Justiciability & Review Audit: Fully justiciable; the Court assumed jurisdiction via the administrative letter referral of the Presiding Justice following a CA En Banc resolution. The matter involved no advisory opinion, but an active, catastrophic breakdown of judicial discipline requiring institutional intervention.
### 7. Separate Opinions & Overall Verdict (Fallo)
**Separate Opinions Summary:**
No separate opinions filed. The decision is **Per Curiam** for the Court En Banc. The main text details the internal voting divisions on specific penalties:
 On Justice Roxas: 12 Justices voted for Dismissal; 1 voted for 6 months suspension.
 On Justice Sabio: 10 Justices voted for 2 months suspension without pay; 1 voted for 6 months suspension; 1 voted for reprimand (as a whistleblower); 1 voted for dismissal.
 On Justice Reyes: 8 Justices voted for Reprimand; 5 voted for 1 month suspension.
 On PJ Vasquez and Justice Dimaranan-Vidal: Voting was unanimous.
**Verbatim Fallo:**
**WHEREFORE**, the Court **RESOLVES** as follows:

(1) Associate Justice Vicente Q. Roxas is found guilty of multiple violations of the canons of the Code of Judicial Conduct, grave misconduct, dishonesty, undue interest and conduct prejudicial to the best interest of the service, and is **DISMISSED** from the service, with **FORFEITURE** of all benefits, except accrued leave credits if any, with prejudice to his re-employment in any branch or service of the government including government-owned and controlled corporations;

(2) Associate Justice Jose L. Sabio, Jr. is found guilty of simple misconduct and conduct unbecoming of a justice of the Court of Appeals and is **SUSPENDED** for two (2) months without pay, with a stern warning that a repetition of the same or similar acts will warrant a more severe penalty;

(3) Presiding Justice Conrado M. Vasquez, Jr. is **SEVERELY REPRIMANDED** for his failure to act promptly and decisively in order to avert the incidents that damaged the image of the Court of Appeals, with a stern warning that a repetition of the same or similar acts will warrant a more severe penalty;

(4) Associate Justice Bienvenido L. Reyes is found guilty of simple misconduct with mitigating circumstance and is **REPRIMANDED**, with a stern warning that a repetition of the same or similar acts will warrant a more severe penalty;

(5) Associate Justice Myrna Dimaranan-Vidal is found guilty of conduct unbecoming a Justice of the Court of Appeals and is **ADMONISHED** to be more circumspect in the discharge of her judicial duties.

(6) PCGG Chairman Camilo L. Sabio's act to influence the judgment of a member of the Judiciary in a pending case is hereby referred to the Bar Confidant for appropriate action;

(7) Justice Jose L. Sabio, Jr.'s charge against Mr. Francis R. De Borja for attempted bribery of a member of the Judiciary is hereby referred to the Department of Justice for appropriate action.

This Decision shall take effect immediately.

**SO ORDERED.**
**Plain-Language Outcome:** The Supreme Court cleansed the Court of Appeals by dismissing Justice Roxas with forfeiture of all benefits, suspending Justice Sabio for two months, severely reprimanding Presiding Justice Vasquez, reprimanding Justice Reyes, and admonishing Justice Dimaranan-Vidal. In addition, the Court referred PCGG Chairman Sabio to the Bar Confidant for disciplinary action as a member of the bar, and referred Francis De Borja to the DOJ for criminal prosecution for attempted bribery.
