### 1. Case Header & Citation Block **Concise Recognizable Title: Yu Oh v. Court of Appeals** **Full Official Caption: Elvira Yu Oh, Petitioner, v. Court of Appeals and People of the Philippines, Respondents.** **Citation & Metadata:** **G.R. No.:** 125297 **Date of Promulgation:** June 6, 2003 **Ponente:** Austria-Martinez, **J.** **Voting Breakdown:** Second Division (Bellosillo, Quisumbing, and Callejo, Sr., **JJ.**, concur). Unanimous; no separate concurring or dissenting opinions. 2. StatCon Diagnostic Matrix & Governing Provision Breakdown Primary StatCon Classification: 1. Statutory Definition / Scope of Penal Statutes: **Subject-Matter Scope** → Meaning of "Penal Laws" under Article 22, Revised Penal Code → Laws conferring court jurisdiction vs. penal laws defining crimes and penalties. 2. Intrinsic Aids & General Statutory Maxims: **Verba Legis** / Principle of Non-Distinction → **Ubi lex non distinguit nec nos distinguere debemus** (Where the law does not distinguish, we ought not to distinguish) → Scope of "any check" and "does not have sufficient funds in or credit" under Section 1, B.P. Blg. 22 (inclusion of postdated checks and "account closed"). 3. Strict Procedural/Substantive Presumption in Penal Laws: Statutory Presumption of Knowledge → Section 2, B.P. Blg. 22 → Mandatory condition precedent of receipt of notice of dishonor → Procedural due process strictly construed against the State. The Contested Statutory / Constitutional Text (Verbatim): A. Article 22, Act No. 3815 (Revised Penal Code) "ART. 22. **Retroactive effect of penal laws.** — **Penal laws** shall have a retroactive effect insofar as they favor the person guilty of a felony, who is not a habitual criminal, as this term is defined in Rule 5 of Article 62 of this Code, although at the time of the publication of such laws a final sentence has been pronounced and the convict is serving sentence." B. Section 1, Batas Pambansa Blg. 22 (Bouncing Checks Law) "SECTION 1. **Checks without sufficient funds.** — Any person who makes or draws and issues **any check** to apply on account or for value, knowing at the time of issue that he **does not have sufficient funds in or credit with the drawee bank** for the payment of such check in full upon its presentment, which check is subsequently dishonored by the drawee bank for **insufficiency of funds or credit** or would have been dishonored for the same reason had not the drawer, without any valid reason, ordered the bank to stop payment, shall be punished by imprisonment of not less than thirty days but not more than one (1) year or by a fine of not less than but not more than double the amount of the check which fine shall in no case exceed Two Hundred Thousand Pesos, or both such fine and imprisonment at the discretion of the court. The same penalty shall be imposed upon any person who, having sufficient funds in or credit with the drawee bank when he makes or draws and issues a check, shall fail to keep sufficient funds or to maintain a credit to cover the full amount of the check if presented within a period of ninety (90) days from the date appeared thereon, for which reason it is dishonored by the drawee bank." ### C. Section 2, Batas Pambansa Blg. 22 "SEC. 2. **Evidence of knowledge of insufficient funds.** — The making, drawing and issuance of a check payment of which is refused by the drawee because of insufficient funds in or credit with such bank, when presented within ninety (90) days from the date of the check, shall be **prima facie** evidence of knowledge of such insufficiency of funds or credit unless such maker or drawer pays the holder thereof the amount due thereon, or makes arrangements for payment in full by the drawee of such check **within five (5) banking days after receiving notice that such check has not been paid by the drawee**." Historical / Amendment Tracking: **B.P. Blg. 129, as amended by Republic Act No. 7691 (Effective June 15, 1994):** **Prior Rule under B.P. Blg. 129:** Regional Trial Courts exercised exclusive original jurisdiction over offenses punishable with imprisonment exceeding four (4) years and two (2) months. BP 22 cases were filed and tried before the RTC. **Amendment under Section 2, R.A. No. 7691:** Metropolitan Trial Courts, Municipal Trial Courts, and Municipal Circuit Trial Courts were vested with exclusive original jurisdiction over all offenses punishable with imprisonment not exceeding six (6) years, irrespective of the amount of fine. **Section 7, R.A. No. 7691:** Contained an express transitional/retroactivity clause limited exclusively to pending **civil cases** that had not yet reached the pre-trial stage. StatCon Diagnostic Profile: **The Linguistic / Interpretive Defects:** 1. **Classification Defect:** Whether the phrase "penal laws" in Article 22 of the Revised Penal Code can be interpreted to subsume jurisdictional statutes (R.A. No. 7691) expanding lower court criminal jurisdiction. 2. **Latent Ambiguity / Alleged Casus Omissus:** Whether the statutory phrasing "any check" and "insufficiency of funds or credit" in Section 1 of B.P. Blg. 22 omits "postdated checks" and "closed accounts," thereby requiring strict construction in favor of the accused to exclude them. 3. **Statutory Prerequisite:** Whether the statutory presumption under Section 2 of B.P. Blg. 22 strictly mandates actual receipt of notice of dishonor where the check's dishonor reason is "Account Closed." **Was Statutory Construction Legally Permissible?:** **As to R.A. No. 7691 & Art. 22, RPC:** No room for construction. A statute defining jurisdiction is substantive law, not a penal law; the plain language of Section 7 of R.A. No. 7691 expressly limits retroactivity to civil cases. **As to "any check" and "closed accounts" in B.P. Blg. 22:** Statutory construction was resolved through the plain and comprehensive text—**ubi lex non distinguit nec nos distinguere debemus**. The law does not distinguish between kinds of checks. **As to Section 2 of B.P. Blg. 22:** Literal application of the statutory requirement of notice of dishonor (**verba legis**) was strictly applied as an indispensable element for triggering the presumption of criminal knowledge. **Controlling Canons / Maxims Deployed:** **Ubi lex non distinguit nec nos distinguere debemus** (Where the law does not distinguish, we ought not to distinguish). **Adherence to Plain Statutory Meaning (Verba Legis)** regarding the 5-day notice requirement under Section 2, B.P. Blg. 22. **Rule of Substantive Jurisdiction:** Jurisdiction is determined by the law in force at the time of the commencement of the action. **Rule on Strict Construction of Penal Statutes** concerning procedural due process and the presumption of innocence. **Factual Interpretive Trigger:** The prosecution of an issuer of 10 postdated checks that bounced due to "Account Closed," where the RTC convicted her despite the passage of R.A. No. 7691 during appeal and despite the lack of proof that a notice of dishonor was ever served upon or received by her. 3. Cast of Characters & Procedural Posture **Key Parties & Roles:** **Elvira Yu Oh:** Petitioner/Accused; buyer of jewelry who issued 10 postdated checks of ₱50,000.00 each pursuant to a court-approved compromise agreement. **Solid Gold International Traders, Inc. (represented by General Manager Joaquin Novales III):** Private Complainant/Creditor to whom the postdated checks were issued and delivered. **People of the Philippines:** Public Respondent, represented by the Office of the Solicitor General (OSG). **Procedural History & Vehicle:** **Inception:** Solid Gold sued petitioner for specific performance in RTC Pasig; parties executed a compromise agreement. Petitioner issued 10 postdated checks drawn on Equitable Banking Corporation (EBC), Grace Park Branch. **Prosecution:** Checks were dishonored upon presentment with the reason "Account Closed." Novales filed 10 Informations for B.P. Blg. 22 before the RTC of Quezon City (Criminal Cases Nos. 92-26243 to 92-36252) on October 5, 1992. **Trial Court:** On December 22, 1993, RTC Quezon City (Branch 99) convicted petitioner on all 10 counts, sentencing her to one year imprisonment per count (totaling 10 years, subject to Art. 70, RPC) and ordering ₱500,000.00 civil indemnity. **Court of Appeals (CA-G.R. CR No. 16390):** On January 30, 1996, the CA affirmed the RTC **in toto**, denying reconsideration on May 30, 1996. The CA held that R.A. No. 7691 could not retroactively divest the RTC of jurisdiction, that postdated checks and closed accounts fall under B.P. Blg. 22, and that notice of dishonor was dispensable because petitioner already knew her account was closed. **Supreme Court Review:** Petition for Review on Certiorari under Rule 45. The Supreme Court reversed and acquitted petitioner due to the prosecution's failure to prove receipt of notice of dishonor. ### 4. Chronological Facts Storyboard 1. **Jewelry Transactions & Civil Compromise:** Petitioner Elvira Yu Oh purchased jewelry from Solid Gold International Traders, Inc. Failing to pay the purchase price, Solid Gold initiated civil actions for specific performance before RTC Pasig (Civil Cases Nos. 58907–59366). 2. **September 17, 1990:** Petitioner and Solid Gold (via GM Joaquin Novales III) entered into a court-approved compromise agreement. Petitioner agreed to issue 99 postdated checks for ₱50,000.00 each, dated every 15th and 30th of the month starting October 1, 1990, plus a lump sum over ₱1 Million on November 16, 1994. 3. **Issuance & Dishonor of Ten Checks:** Petitioner issued 10 checks of ₱50,000.00 each (totaling ₱500,000.00) drawn against Equitable Banking Corporation (EBC), Grace Park, Caloocan City Branch. Novales deposited them on their due dates with Far East Bank and Trust Company (FEBTC). All 10 checks were returned dishonored stamped with "Account Closed." 4. **October 5, 1992:** Novales initiated criminal complaints. Ten separate Informations for violation of B.P. Blg. 22 were filed before RTC Quezon City. 5. **Trial and Conviction:** Accused pleaded not guilty. During trial, the prosecution presented dishonor slips sent to **Solid Gold** (Exhibits "D-2" to "L-2", "C-2"), but presented no evidence of notice sent to or received by petitioner. Novales testified that he made no personal demands upon petitioner prior to filing charges. The trial court relied on petitioner's counter-affidavit where she noted that she told Solid Gold upon issuance that the checks might not be covered by funds. 6. **December 22, 1993:** RTC Quezon City rendered a judgment of conviction on all 10 counts. 7. **June 15, 1994:** Republic Act No. 7691 took effect, expanding the jurisdiction of Metropolitan/Municipal Trial Courts to offenses punishable with imprisonment up to 6 years. 8. **January 30, 1996:** The Court of Appeals affirmed the conviction, ruling that R.A. No. 7691 did not apply retroactively to divest the RTC of jurisdiction and that notice of dishonor was superfluous because an issuer who closes her account cannot expect checks to be honored. 9. **June 6, 2003:** The Supreme Court reversed the CA and acquitted petitioner of criminal liability while sustaining civil liability. 5. Competing Interpretations Matrix (The Clash of Canons) | Provision / Concept | Petitioner's Interpretation | Respondent's / Court's Interpretation | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Article 22, RPC vis-à-vis R.A. No. 7691** | **Petitioner:** R.A. No. 7691 is a "penal law" because it affects the court's jurisdiction over criminal cases. Under Art. 22, RPC, it must apply retroactively to benefit the accused, placing jurisdiction exclusively in the MTC and voiding the RTC judgment.
**Canons:** Rule on Retroactivity of Benignant Penal Laws (Art. 22, RPC); Strict construction against the State. | **Respondent / Court:** R.A. No. 7691 is a substantive jurisdictional law, not a penal law; it does not define crimes or fix penalties. Substantive laws governing jurisdiction apply prospectively from commencement of action.
**Canons:** Plain Meaning Rule (**Verba Legis**); Expressio Unius (Sec. 7 of R.A. 7691 limits retroactivity to pending civil cases); **Cang v. CA** doctrine. | | **Section 1, B.P. Blg. 22 ("Any check" & "Closed Accounts")** | **Petitioner:** B.P. Blg. 22 only penalizes checks dishonored for "insufficiency" of funds, not "closed accounts" or "no funds." Furthermore, postdated checks are not payable on demand under Sec. 185, NIL, but are ordinary bills of exchange; applying B.P. Blg. 22 to them is judicial legislation.
**Canons:** Strict construction of penal statutes; Plain meaning of "insufficiency." | **Respondent / Court:** "Closed accounts" is subsumed under "does not have sufficient funds in or credit." The statutory term "any check" is broad and unqualified, covering present-dated and postdated checks.
**Canons: Ubi lex non distinguit nec nos distinguere debemus**; Broad statutory terms; Legislative intent to preserve commercial stream and suppress worthless checks. | | **Section 2, B.P. Blg. 22 (Notice of Dishonor)** | **Petitioner:** Notice of dishonor is an indispensable statutory element under Sec. 2 to activate the **prima facie** presumption of knowledge. Deprivation of notice violates procedural due process and eliminates the 5-day period to pay.
**Canons:** Mandatory statutory condition precedent; Presumption of innocence; Strict adherence to statutory elements. | **Respondent (CA / OSG):** Notice of dishonor is dispensable where the account is closed, as the drawer already knows the check will bounce; demanding notice would be an empty formality.
**Court's Rejection:** Notice is mandatory. The law makes no exception. Knowledge of closed account cannot dispense with the statutory 5-day grace period to avert prosecution. | 6. Inventory of Statutory Construction & Substantive Issues 1. **[PRIMARY STATCON ISSUE]** Whether Republic Act No. 7691 is a "penal law" within the purview of Article 22 of the Revised Penal Code so as to warrant its retroactive application to divest the Regional Trial Court of jurisdiction over pending criminal cases. **Faithful Court Formulation:** "Whether or not the appellate court erred in not giving retroactive effect to R.A. 7690 [7691] in view of Article 22 of the RPC." **Recit-Ready StatCon Question:** Does the term "penal laws" in Article 22 of the Revised Penal Code include an amendatory statute expanding the trial jurisdiction of inferior courts (R.A. No. 7691), thereby requiring its retroactive application to void an RTC conviction? 2. **[PRIMARY STATCON ISSUE]** Whether the phrase "any check" and the clause "does not have sufficient funds in or credit with the drawee bank" under Section 1 of B.P. Blg. 22 exclude postdated checks and checks dishonored by reason of "Account Closed." **Faithful Court Formulation:** "Whether or not the appellate court erroneously construed B.P. Blg. 22." **Recit-Ready StatCon Question:** Under the maxim **ubi lex non distinguit nec nos distinguere debemus**, does Section 1 of B.P. Blg. 22 penalize the issuance of postdated checks subsequently dishonored for "Account Closed," or is its scope strictly confined to present-dated checks dishonored for mere "insufficiency of funds"? 3. **[Substantive / Constitutional Issue]** Whether the receipt of a notice of dishonor by the drawer under Section 2 of B.P. Blg. 22 is an indispensable prerequisite to establish criminal liability, even if the drawee bank dishonored the checks due to "Account Closed." **Faithful Court Formulation:** "Whether or not notice of dishonor is dispensable in this case." **Recit-Ready StatCon Question:** Can the statutory requirement of notice of dishonor under Section 2 of B.P. Blg. 22 be judicially dispensed with where the drawer's bank account is already closed at presentment? ### 7. Deep-Dive Verdict, Tool Analysis, & Ratio Decidendi per Issue ISSUE 1: Retroactivity of R.A. No. 7691 under Article 22 of the Revised Penal Code **(a) Issue & Short Answer: NO.** Republic Act No. 7691 is a substantive statute defining court jurisdiction, not a penal law, and cannot be applied retroactively to divest the trial court of criminal jurisdiction properly acquired at the time the Informations were filed. **(b) Verbatim Doctrinal & Canons Pronouncements:** "A penal law, as defined by this Court, is an act of the legislature that prohibits certain acts and establishes penalties for its violations. It also defines crime, treats of its nature and provides for its punishment. R.A. No. 7691 does not prohibit certain acts or provides penalties for its violation; neither does it treat of the nature of crimes and its punishment. Consequently, R.A. No. 7691 is not a penal law, and therefore, Art. 22 of the RPC does not apply in the present case." "In the case of **Cang vs. Court of Appeals**, this Court held that 'jurisdiction being a matter of substantive law, the established rule is that the statute in force at the time of the commencement of the action determines the jurisdiction of the court.' R.A. No. 7691 was not yet in force at the time of the commencement of the cases in the trial court... The Court has held that a 'law vesting additional jurisdiction in the court cannot be given retroactive effect.'" **(c) Step-by-Step Interpretative Reasoning:** 1. **Threshold Gate:** The Court analyzed the definitive legal meaning of "penal laws" under Article 22 of the RPC. Finding no ambiguity, it held that Article 22 applies strictly to statutes defining crimes and fixing punishments. 2. **Intrinsic Aids Examined:** The Court examined the title and subject matter of R.A. No. 7691 ("**An Act Expanding the Jurisdiction of the Municipal Trial Courts, Municipal Circuit Trial Courts and the Metropolitan Trial Court...**"). Section 7 was reviewed, revealing an express legislative intent restricting retroactive application exclusively to pending **civil cases** that had not reached the pre-trial stage. 3. **Statutory Presumptions & Policies:** The Court applied the well-settled principle of jurisdiction: substantive jurisdiction over criminal cases is conferred by the statute in force at the time of the commencement of the action (filing of the Information). Jurisdiction, once acquired, adheres until final termination. 4. **Rejection of Losing Construction:** The Court rejected petitioner's argument that procedural/jurisdictional statutes affecting criminal offenses constitute benignant penal laws under Article 22, RPC. Because R.A. No. 7691 neither creates an offense nor mitigates a penalty, it cannot operate retroactively to divest the RTC of jurisdiction. **(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation:** **(Plain-Language StatCon Explanation)** R.A. No. 7691 is a law defining court jurisdiction, not a penal law that defines crimes or reduces penalties. Consequently, Article 22 of the Revised Penal Code cannot be invoked to give it retroactive effect to nullify an RTC conviction that was validly commenced before R.A. No. 7691 took effect. ISSUE 2: Scope of B.P. Blg. 22 ("Any Check" and "Account Closed") **(a) Issue & Short Answer: NO (Appellate Court Did Not Err).** The statutory language of B.P. Blg. 22 is comprehensive and applies to all checks, whether present-dated or postdated, and the phrase "insufficient funds" encompasses "closed accounts" or "no funds." **(b) Verbatim Doctrinal & Canons Pronouncements:** "B.P. Blg. 22 ... does not distinguish but merely provides that '[a]ny person who makes or draws and issues any check knowing at the time of issue that he does not have sufficient funds in or credit with the drawee bank ... which check is subsequently dishonored ... shall be punished by imprisonment ...' **Ubi lex non distinguit nec nos distinguere debemus**." "The term 'closed accounts' is within the meaning of the phrase 'does not have sufficient funds in or credit with the drawee bank'." "This Court, in **Lozano vs. Martinez**, was explicit in ruling that the language of B.P. Blg. 22 is broad enough to cover all kinds of checks, whether present dated or postdated, or whether issued in payment of pre-existing obligations or given in mutual or simultaneous exchange for something of value." **(c) Step-by-Step Interpretative Reasoning:** 1. **Threshold Gate:** The Court applied the literal, broad text of Section 1 of B.P. Blg. 22. The statute uses the categorical and unqualified phrase "any check." 2. **Controlling Latin Maxim:** The Court explicitly invoked **Ubi lex non distinguit nec nos distinguere debemus** (Where the law does not distinguish, we ought not to distinguish). Since the statute does not exempt postdated checks or differentiate between zero balance ("closed account") and partial deficiency ("insufficient funds"), the courts cannot create distinctions. 3. **Intrinsic Aids & Legislative Intent:** Drawing from legislative history traced in **Lozano v. Martinez** and **People v. Nitafan**, the Court noted that the Batasang Pambansa intended the concept of "check" to be all-inclusive. A closed account is mathematically and logically the ultimate form of insufficient funds. 4. **Statutory Purpose / Mischief Rule:** The public policy of B.P. Blg. 22 is to protect public order, trade, and the banking system from worthless commercial paper. Exempting postdated checks or closed accounts would defeat the statutory objective. **(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation:** **(Plain-Language StatCon Explanation)** Under the maxim **ubi lex non distinguit nec nos distinguere debemus**, the statutory term "any check" includes postdated checks, and a "closed account" is covered under the phrase "insufficient funds." Courts cannot carve out exceptions that the legislature did not write into the text of B.P. Blg. 22. ISSUE 3: Mandatory Requirement of Notice of Dishonor under Section 2, B.P. Blg. 22 **(a) Issue & Short Answer: NO (Notice is NOT Dispensable).** Service and actual receipt of a notice of dishonor upon the maker/drawer are indispensable statutory prerequisites to create the **prima facie** presumption of knowledge of insufficient funds; absent proof of receipt, conviction cannot stand. **(b) Verbatim Doctrinal & Canons Pronouncements:** "Based on this section, the presumption that the issuer had knowledge of the insufficiency of funds is brought into existence **only after it is proved that the issuer had received a notice of dishonor** and that within five days from receipt thereof, he failed to pay the amount of the check or to make arrangement for its payment. The presumption or **prima facie** evidence as provided in this section cannot arise, if such notice of non-payment by the drawee bank is not sent to the maker or drawer, or if there is no proof as to when such notice was received by the drawer, since there would simply be no way of reckoning the crucial 5-day period." "Indeed, this requirement cannot be taken lightly because Section 2 provides for an opportunity for the drawer to effect full payment of the amount appearing on the check, within five banking days **from notice of dishonor**. The absence of said notice therefore deprives an accused of an opportunity to preclude criminal prosecution. In other words, procedural due process demands that a notice of dishonor be actually served on petitioner." "... [I]t is essential for the maker or drawer to be notified of the dishonor of her check, so she could pay the value thereof or make arrangements for its payment within the period prescribed by law' and omission or neglect on the part of the prosecution to prove that the accused received such notice of dishonor is fatal to its cause." **(c) Step-by-Step Interpretative Reasoning:** 1. **Threshold Gate:** Section 2 of B.P. Blg. 22 explicitly sets forth the statutory conditions for the presumption of knowledge: (a) dishonor upon presentment within 90 days; and (b) failure to pay or arrange for payment within five banking days **after receiving notice** of dishonor. 2. **Strict Construction in Favor of Due Process:** The statutory 5-day grace period is a complete substantive defense provided by law to abort criminal liability. Therefore, actual receipt of notice is not a mere technicality but an indispensable element of procedural due process. 3. **Rejection of CA and Solicitor General's Argument:** The CA held that notice was superfluous because the account was closed. The Supreme Court rejected this, holding that Section 2 admits of no exception. Knowledge that an account is closed does not strip the drawer of the statutory right to be given 5 banking days from notice to make good the check and avoid criminal indictment. 4. **Failure of Quantum of Proof:** While the prosecution produced dishonor slips, they were addressed and delivered solely to the payee (Solid Gold), not petitioner. The lack of proof beyond reasonable doubt of service and receipt of notice destroyed the **prima facie** presumption of knowledge, necessitating an acquittal. **(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation:** **(Plain-Language StatCon Explanation)** Section 2 of B.P. Blg. 22 requires proof that the drawer actually received a notice of dishonor, giving her five banking days to pay and prevent criminal liability. Even if an account is closed, the court cannot dispense with this statutory notice requirement, because doing so deprives the accused of procedural due process and the presumption of innocence. 8. Separate Opinions on Statutory Construction **No separate opinions discussed in the provided text.** 9. Overall Verdict (Dispositive Portion / Fallo) **Verbatim Dispositive Portion:** "WHEREFORE, the assailed Decision and Resolution of the Court of Appeals are hereby REVERSED and SET ASIDE. Petitioner Elvira Yu Oh is ACQUITTED of the offense of violation of B.P. Blg. 22 on ten counts for insufficiency of evidence. However, she is ordered to pay complainant Solid Gold International Traders, Inc. the total amount of Five Hundred Thousand Pesos (₱500,000.00) with 12% interest per annum from date of finality of herein judgment. SO ORDERED." **Plain-Language Outcome:** Petitioner Elvira Yu Oh was completely acquitted of all ten criminal counts of violating B.P. Blg. 22 because the prosecution failed to prove that she ever received notices of dishonor, which are statutory prerequisites under Section 2. However, her civil obligation remains valid, and she was ordered to pay Solid Gold ₱500,000.00 plus 12% legal interest per annum upon finality of the judgment.

digest:
### 1. Case Header & Citation Block
**Concise Recognizable Title: Philippine Consumers Foundation, Inc. v. National Telecommunications Commission**
**Full Official Caption:** Philippine Consumers Foundation, Inc., Petitioner, vs. National Telecommunications Commission and Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co., Respondents.
**Citation & Metadata:**
G.R. No. L-63318
Promulgation Date: August 18, 1984 (Resolution on Second Motion for Reconsideration)
Ponente: Makasiar, J.
Voting Breakdown: En Banc.
**Concurring:** Concepcion, Jr., Guerrero, Escolin, De la Fuente, and Cuevas, JJ., concurred with the ponencia of Makasiar, J.
**Concurring in the result:** Aquino and Plana, JJ.
**Separate Concurring Opinion:** Gutierrez, Jr., J.
**Took No Part:** Fernando, C.J.
**Dissenting Opinions:** Teehankee, J.; Abad Santos, J. (joined by Melencio-Herrera, J.); Relova, J. (joined by Melencio-Herrera, J.).
2. StatCon Diagnostic Matrix & Governing Provision Breakdown
**Primary StatCon Classification:**
**Statutory Construction Area:** Verba Legis / Plain Meaning Rule → Permissive vs. Mandatory Statutory Terms.
**Specific Canon / Principle Applied:** Preserving the ordinary distinction between "may" and "shall" when juxtaposed within the same statutory sentence; refusal to construe a discretionary grant of authority as a mandatory condition precedent.
**Specific Latin Maxim:** Identified in dissent as **a verba legis non est recedendum** (from the words of the statute there should be no departure) / **index animi sermo est** (speech is the index of intention).
**Specific Sub-Issue:** Whether the phrase "pertinent rules and regulations may be promulgated" creates a mandatory duty and jurisdictional prerequisite that bars administrative action until implementing rules are issued, or whether it merely confers permissive, discretionary rule-making authority alongside existing procedural and substantive public utility law.
**The Contested Statutory / Constitutional Text (Verbatim):**
**Section 2, Presidential Decree No. 217:**
"The Department of Public Works, Transportation and Communications, through its Board of Communications and/or appropriate agency **shall** see to it that the herein declared policies for the telephone industry are immediately implemented and for this purpose, pertinent rules and regulations **may be promulgated**."
**Historical / Amendment Tracking:**
**P.D. No. 217, Section 2 (Promulgated June 16, 1973):** Evaluated above.
**P.D. No. 1874 (Promulgated July 21, 1983 - Amending P.D. No. 217):**
Amended Section 6 to re-calculate the 50% limit and provided: **"PROVIDED, however, that the amount payable by the telephone subscriber may be paid on installment or under such payment arrangement as the National Telecommunications Commission may authorize."**
Clarified the power of the NTC to approve provisional rate increases: **"[A]uthorizes the National Telecommunications Commission... to approve 'such amounts for subscriber investments as applied for provisionally and without the necessity of a hearing; but shall call a hearing thereon within thirty (30) days thereafter, upon publication and notice to all parties affected.'"**
**StatCon Diagnostic Profile:**
**The Linguistic / Interpretive Defect:** Plain Meaning vs. Strained Judicial Construction. Petitioner and the original majority opinion imputed a mandatory, condition-precedent requirement to the permissive modal auxiliary "may be promulgated."
**Was Statutory Construction Legally Permissible?:** Construction converting "may" to "shall" was ruled impermissible. The Court held that words must be given their ordinary, plain meaning; where the text uses "may," it cannot be distorted into "shall" or "must" absent an explicit contrary legislative mandate.
**Controlling Canon / Maxim Deployed: Verba legis** (ordinary meaning of words); plain semantic distinction between the mandatory "shall" and the permissive/discretionary "may" when deployed within the exact same statutory sentence.
**Factual Interpretive Trigger:** The NTC approved the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Company's (PLDT) revised Subscriber Investments Plan (SIP) schedule of rates without having first promulgated a discrete set of new implementing rules and regulations under Section 2 of P.D. No. 217.
3. Cast of Characters & Procedural Posture
**Key Parties & Roles:**
**Philippine Consumers Foundation, Inc. (PCFI):** Petitioner consumer advocacy group; oppositor to PLDT's revised investment rates.
**National Telecommunications Commission (NTC):** Public respondent; administrative regulatory agency governing telecommunications utilities (successor to the Board of Communications and Public Service Commission).
**Philippine Long Distance Telephone Company (PLDT):** Private respondent telephone utility firm; applicant for an upward revision of its SIP rates.
**Solicitor General:** Counsel for public respondent NTC, who initially joined in the oppositions during initial hearings, but ultimately defended NTC and joined PLDT's motion for reconsideration.
**Procedural History & Vehicle:**
**Administrative Level:** PLDT filed an application to revise its SIP schedule on March 20, 1980 before the NTC (NTC Case No. 82-87). NTC provisionally approved it on April 14, 1982. The Supreme Court set aside that provisional approval in **Samuel Bautista v. NTC** (116 SCRA 411) for lack of hearing. On remand, NTC held five hearings with full cross-examination. On November 22, 1982, NTC approved the revised SIP rates; on January 14, 1983, it denied reconsideration.
**Original SC Petition:** PCFI filed a Petition for Certiorari under Rule 65 to annul the November 22, 1982 Decision and January 14, 1983 Order. On November 25, 1983, the Supreme Court (by a 9-member majority, with 3 taking no part and 1 reserving vote) granted the petition and annulled the NTC rulings on the premise that NTC was required to first promulgate rules under P.D. No. 217.
**Review on Reconsideration:** PLDT filed a Motion for Reconsideration, followed by a Supplemental Motion for Reconsideration (adopted by NTC). The Court initially denied reconsideration on April 3, 1984 (without stating the denial was final). PLDT obtained leave and filed a Second Motion for Reconsideration (again adopted by NTC).
**Supreme Court En Banc Action:** Reconsidered and set aside the November 25, 1983 Decision; dismissed the petition; affirmed the NTC's approval of the revised SIP schedule.
### 4. Chronological Facts Storyboard
1. **June 16, 1973:** P.D. No. 217 is enacted, establishing the policy of telephone subscriber self-financing (allowing up to 50% of installation costs to be funded by subscriber investment through stock ownership).
2. **January 25, 1978:** The Board of Communications (BOC, predecessor to NTC) promulgates Rules of Practice and Procedure pursuant to Section 11 of the Public Service Act (C.A. No. 146).
3. **March 20, 1980:** PLDT files an application with the NTC to increase and revise its SIP schedule of rates.
4. **April 14, 1982:** NTC provisionally approves the revised SIP schedule without a prior hearing.
5. **August 31, 1982:** In **Samuel Bautista v. NTC** (116 SCRA 411), the Supreme Court sets aside the April 14, 1982 order, holding that a hearing was required before the Commission could act on PLDT's application, to give oppositors an opportunity to challenge the rates as excessive.
6. **August 1982 to Late 1982:** In NTC Case No. 82-87, NTC conducts five hearings. Petitioner PCFI, the Solicitor General, and others file written oppositions. Applicant PLDT presents its Vice-President for Budget and Financial Planning, who is thoroughly cross-examined. None of the oppositors present evidence; they submit memoranda and submit the case for decision.
7. **November 22, 1982:** NTC renders its Decision approving the revised SIP schedule, finding the rates to be within the 50% cost limit under P.D. No. 217, just, reasonable, and in the public interest.
8. **January 14, 1983:** NTC denies petitioner’s motion for reconsideration.
9. **March 2, 1983:** PCFI files a petition for certiorari with the Supreme Court.
10. **July 21, 1983:** P.D. No. 1874 is promulgated, amending P.D. No. 217 to confirm provisional rate approval powers and provide installment arrangements.
11. **November 25, 1983:** The Supreme Court promulgates its original decision annulling the NTC decision and order, ruling that the promulgation of rules under Section 2 of P.D. No. 217 was mandatory prior to approving SIP schedules.
12. **January 12, 1984 to May 2, 1984:** PLDT and NTC file motions and supplemental motions for reconsideration. An initial denial on April 3, 1984 (not marked final) is succeeded by leave to file a Second Motion for Reconsideration on May 2, 1984.
13. **August 18, 1984:** The Supreme Court En Banc grants the Second Motion for Reconsideration, overturns the November 25, 1983 Decision, and dismisses the PCFI petition.
5. Competing Interpretations Matrix (The Clash of Canons)
A. Petitioner's Interpretation (Adopted in the Overturned November 25, 1983 Decision and Dissents)
**Core Reading:** The phrase "pertinent rules and regulations may be promulgated" in Section 2 of P.D. No. 217 must be construed as **mandatory** ("shall" or "must"). Promulgating such rules and regulations is an indispensable condition precedent before the NTC can acquire jurisdiction or authority to approve SIP rate schedules.
**Canons, Aids, & Maxims Invoked:**
**Subservience of Words to Intent (verba intentioni, non e contra, debent inservire):** Permissive words will be construed as mandatory when the statute relates to public duty, justice, or concerns public interest.
**Sutherland Statutory Construction Rule on Mandatory "May":** Where an act creates power touching the rights of individuals or the public good, the execution of the power is a duty.
**Sui Generis / Novel Subject Matter Exception:** P.D. No. 217 introduced an unprecedented, innovative self-financing concept; hence, existing procedural mechanisms under C.A. No. 146 cannot govern.
**Policy / Consequence Argument:** Approving massive equity extractions from captive utility subscribers in the absence of explicit, formal implementing regulations creates outright confusion regarding consumer rights, invites arbitrary corporate extraction, and constitutes an unreasonable imposition by a monopoly whose service is deficient.
B. Respondent's Interpretation (Adopted by the Court in the August 18, 1984 Resolution)
**Core Reading:** "May be promulgated" is purely **permissive and discretionary**. Promulgation of administrative rules is not a condition precedent to the exercise of quasi-judicial jurisdiction to approve SIP rates.
**Canons, Aids, & Maxims Invoked:**
**Verba Legis / Plain Meaning Rule:** Words must be given their ordinary and customary meaning unless a contrary legislative intent is manifest. "May" denotes discretion; "shall" denotes command.
**Intra-Sentence Juxtaposition Canon:** When the legislature uses both "shall" ("shall see to it...") and "may" ("may be promulgated") within the very same sentence, it purposefully preserves and highlights the grammatical distinction between mandatory duty and permissive discretion.
**Doctrine of Non-Repeal by Implication / Harmonization:** Section 3 of P.D. No. 217 only repeals laws inconsistent with it. The Public Service Act (C.A. No. 146, as amended) and the 1978 Board of Communications Rules remain active and fully supply the substantive criteria and procedural framework.
**Policy / Consequence Argument:** Telecommunications is highly capital-intensive; capital per unit increases as customer volume expands. Forcing the NTC to freeze all self-financing approvals until separate rules are promulgated frustrates the explicit mandate of P.D. No. 217 for the **immediate implementation** of public utility financing, driving utilities into crushing foreign debt and currency drains.
6. Inventory of Statutory Construction & Substantive Issues
### 1. [PRIMARY STATCON ISSUE]
**Faithful Court Formulation:** Whether the rule-making authority delegated in Section 2 of P.D. No. 217 to the regulatory agency ("pertinent rules and regulations may be promulgated") is mandatory or discretionary.
**Recit-Ready StatCon Question:** Does the phrase "pertinent rules and regulations may be promulgated" in Section 2 of P.D. No. 217 impose a mandatory condition precedent requiring the NTC to issue implementing rules before it can approve a Subscriber Investment Plan, or does the intra-sentence pairing of "shall" and "may" preserve the ordinary permissive meaning of "may"?

digest:
**Faithful Court Formulation:** Whether the NTC acted arbitrarily or contrary to P.D. No. 217 in approving PLDT's revised SIP rate schedule.
### 7. Deep-Dive Verdict, Tool Analysis, & Ratio Decidendi per Issue
Issue 1: [PRIMARY STATCON ISSUE] Discretionary vs. Mandatory Nature of "May Be Promulgated" in Section 2 of P.D. No. 217
(a) Issue & Short Answer
**NO.** The phrase "may be promulgated" is permissive and discretionary, not mandatory; the NTC is not legally required to promulgate new rules and regulations as a prerequisite to exercising its authority to evaluate and approve SIP rates.
(b) Verbatim Doctrinal & Canons Pronouncements
**"The basic canon of statutory interpretation is that the word used in the law must be given its ordinary meaning, unless a contrary intent is manifest from the law itself. Hence, the phrase 'may be promulgated' should not be construed to mean 'shall' or 'must'. It shall be interpreted in its ordinary sense as permissive or discretionary on the part of the delegate..."**
**"There is nothing in P.D. No. 217 which commands that the phrase 'may be promulgated' should be construed as 'shall be promulgated.'"**
**"Both words 'shall' and 'may be' are employed in the lone sentence of Section 2 of P.D. No. 217. This graphically demonstrates that P.D. No. 217 preserves the distinction between their ordinary, usual or nominal senses."**
**"The construction of the majority decision of November 25, 1983 of the word 'may' to mean 'shall' is too strained, if not tortured."**
(c) Step-by-Step Interpretative Reasoning (The Tool Deep-Dive)
1. **Threshold Gate:** The Court closed the gate on judicial interpretation and enforced **verba legis**. When the decree’s language is plain, words must be accepted in their natural, ordinary lexical import without strained judicial construction.
2. Intrinsic Aids Examined:
**Syntactical Structure & Word Juxtaposition:** The Court analyzed the single sentence comprising Section 2: **"The Department... shall see to it that the herein declared policies... are immediately implemented and for this purpose, pertinent rules and regulations may be promulgated."** The immediate contrast between "shall" and "may" within the same sentence establishes that the lawmaker was conscious of the difference between an imperative duty ("shall see to it") and a permissive authority ("may be promulgated").
**Harmonization with the Repealing Clause (Section 3, P.D. No. 217):** Section 3 only repeals provisions of the Public Service Act (C.A. No. 146) **in conflict** with the Decree. Because there was no conflict, the rate-making powers in Section 16(c) of C.A. No. 146 remained operative.
3. Extrinsic Aids Examined:
**Existing Regulatory Framework (Pre-existing Rules):** The Court evaluated the 1978 Rules of Practice and Procedure promulgated by the Board of Communications (NTC's predecessor) and procedural provisions of C.A. No. 146, confirming that an administrative apparatus governing notice, hearing, and rate-setting already existed and was actively utilized.
**Subsequent Clarificatory Legislation (P.D. No. 1874):** The Court observed that P.D. No. 1874, which explicitly allowed provisional approval and installment schemes under P.D. No. 217, served to clarify the seeming ambiguity of the repealing clause in Section 3 and confirmed existing regulatory powers.
4. Statutory Presumptions & Policies:
**Presumption Against Ineffectiveness:** Interpreting "may" as a mandatory bar would paralyze the telephone industry's expansion and violate the decree's primary command: that the declared policies be **immediately implemented**.
**Constitutional Policy Context:** Section 5, Article XIV of the 1973 Constitution mandates that the State encourage equity participation in public utilities by the general public.
5. Rejection of Losing Construction:
The Court rejected petitioner’s position that the NTC lacked jurisdiction absent new rules as an untenable distortion of ordinary language. The Court underscored that **Ang Tibay v. CIR** (69 Phil. 635) established the cardinal requirements of quasi-judicial due process, and the prior promulgation of administrative implementing rules is **not** one of them.
(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation
**(Plain-Language StatCon Explanation)**: Under the basic **verba legis** rule, words are given their natural, ordinary meaning. Because the lawmaker used both "shall" (mandatory) and "may" (permissive) in the very same sentence of Section 2 of P.D. No. 217, it intentionally commanded the immediate execution of the policy while leaving the issuance of new regulations to agency discretion; therefore, "may" cannot be tortured into meaning "shall," and the NTC had full authority to apply existing public utility laws and rules to approve the SIP rate increases.
Issue 2: [Procedural & Due Process Issue] Compliance with Due Process Requirements
(a) Issue & Short Answer
**YES.** The proceedings before the NTC satisfied all administrative due process requirements under the **Ang Tibay** doctrine, as oppositors were given full notice, attended multiple hearings, and extensively cross-examined PLDT’s witnesses.
(b) Verbatim Doctrinal & Canons Pronouncements
**"In Ang Tibay vs. CIR (69 Phil. 635), this Court, through Mr. Justice Jose P. Laurel, did not include the promulgation of rules and regulations as among the seven (7) requirements of due process in quasi-judicial proceedings before a quasi-judicial body such as the respondent NTC."**
**"It is undisputed therefore that petitioner and the other oppositors were accorded due process."**
(c) Step-by-Step Interpretative Reasoning
1. **Factual Compliance with Ang Tibay:** Following the remand ordered in **Samuel Bautista v. NTC**, the NTC set NTC Case No. 82-87 for five hearing dates starting August 4, 1982.
2. **Opportunity to Be Heard:** Oppositors (including PCFI) filed written oppositions and thoroughly cross-examined PLDT’s budget officer.
3. **Waiver of Presentation of Evidence:** Oppositors voluntarily chose not to introduce their own rebuttal evidence and opted to submit the matter on written memoranda.
4. **Conclusion:** Quasi-judicial due process requires notice and an opportunity to explain one's side; it does not require an administrative agency to enact a bespoke administrative code prior to resolving a rate petition.
(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation
**(Plain-Language StatCon Explanation)**: Due process in administrative agencies requires only an opportunity to be heard, notice, and consideration of evidence under the classic **Ang Tibay** standards. Because the NTC conducted formal hearings where the petitioner fully cross-examined PLDT’s witness, the absence of independent implementing regulations did not deprive petitioner of procedural due process.
Issue 3: [Substantive / Constitutional Issue] Substantive Validity of the Revised SIP Schedule
(a) Issue & Short Answer
**YES.** The NTC's approval of the revised SIP schedule was substantively valid, supported by evidence, within the statutory 50% cost ceiling, and aligned with national economic policy.
(b) Verbatim Doctrinal & Canons Pronouncements
**"Respondent NTC rendered the challenged decision dated November 22, 1982, approving the revised schedule on the ground that the rates are within the 50% of cost limit provided in P.D. No. 217, that they are just and reasonable and in consonance with the public policies declared in said decree, and that such approval is in the public interest..."**
**"With the dividends that will be received quarterly under the revised SIP schedule, the subscribers... will recover their investments after some years and will thereafter remain stockholders and part-owners of PLDT. All the subscribers therefore, are assured not only of profits from but also preservation of, their investments, which are not donations to PLDT."**
(c) Step-by-Step Interpretative Reasoning
1. **Substantive Limits of P.D. No. 217:** The statutory self-financing threshold was strictly maintained, as the rates did not exceed 50% of the cost of installation.
2. **Economic Realities & Capital Intensity:** The Court recognized that the telephone industry is uniquely capital-intensive, unit costs rise as the network expands, and reliance on foreign commercial debt threatens national foreign exchange reserves.
3. **Subscriber Return:** Under the SIP model, subscriber payments are not operating fees or donations; they represent capital investments earning regular dividends and convertible to common stock, fulfilling the constitutional aim of broadening public utility ownership.
(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation
**(Plain-Language StatCon Explanation)**: The approved SIP schedule was substantively sound because it remained strictly under the statutory 50% capital ceiling fixed by P.D. No. 217 and converted subscriber cash outlays into income-earning corporate equity, thereby advancing the constitutional and statutory goals of widespread domestic ownership and capital formation.
8. Separate Opinions on Statutory Construction
**Concurring Opinion of Gutierrez, Jr., J.:**
Concurred with the statutory interpretation of the **ponencia** regarding the permissive nature of "may" in Section 2, the sufficiency of existing procedural rules, and the economic policies underlying P.D. Nos. 217 and 1874.
Expressed strong reservations regarding PLDT's chronic service inefficiency, emphasizing that the statutory authorization to demand mandatory equity investment from subscribers carries the regulatory duty to enforce high-quality public service.
**Dissenting Opinion of Abad Santos, J. (joined by Melencio-Herrera, J.):**
**Interpretative Clash:** Challenged the majority's reliance on **a verba legis non est recedendum** and **index animi sermo est**. Countered with the maxim **verba intentioni, non e contra, debent inservire** (words ought to be subservient to the intent, not intent to the words).
**Construction of "May" as Mandatory:** Invoking Black and Sutherland, argued that permissive words like "may" must be construed as mandatory ("shall") when the statute directs an act touching public duty, justice, or the rights of individuals.
**Alien & Innovative Nature:** P.D. No. 217 introduced an unprecedented self-financing scheme that conflicted with the traditional limiting spirit of the Public Service Act; thus, clear regulatory guidelines were an indispensable prerequisite to protect a captive public from monopoly exactions.
**Dissenting Opinion of Relova, J. (joined by Melencio-Herrera, J.):**
Reaffirmed his original November 25, 1983 **ponencia**.
Rejected PLDT's invocation of the amendatory P.D. No. 1874, pointing out that Section 4 explicitly excluded decisions pending review before the Supreme Court on the date of its decree.
**Dissenting Opinion of Teehankee, J.:**
Concurred with the dissents of Abad Santos and Relova, JJ.
Centered on procedural regularity, protesting the overturning of an established decision upon a second motion for reconsideration without setting the case for oral argument.
9. Overall Verdict (Dispositive Portion / Fallo)
**Verbatim Fallo:**
"WHEREFORE, THE DECISION OF NOVEMBER 25, 1983 SHOULD BE AS IT IS HEREBY RECONSIDERED AND SET ASIDE AND THE PETITION IS HEREBY DISMISSED. NO COSTS.
SO ORDERED."
**Plain-Language Outcome:** Private respondent PLDT and public respondent NTC prevailed. The Supreme Court reversed its prior judgment and upheld the NTC's approval of PLDT's revised Subscriber Investments Plan rates, definitively ruling that administrative regulatory agencies are not legally required to issue implementing regulations prior to acting on rate applications where the enabling statute employs the permissive phrase "may be promulgated" and existing procedural mechanisms are adequate.

digest:
### 1. Case Header & Citation Block
**Concise Recognizable Title: Director of Lands v. Court of Appeals** (or **Director of Lands v. Abistado**)
**Full Official Caption:** The Director of Lands, Petitioner, v. Court of Appeals and Teodoro Abistado, substituted by Margarita, Marissa, Maribel, Arnold and Mary Ann, all surnamed Abistado, Respondents.
**Citation & Metadata:**
**G.R. No.:** 102858
**Date of Promulgation:** July 28, 1997
**Ponente:** Panganiban, **J.**
**Voting Breakdown:** Third Division (Unanimous). Davide, Jr., Melo, and Francisco, **JJ.**, concur; Narvasa, **C.J.**, on leave. No separate concurring or dissenting opinions filed.
2. StatCon Diagnostic Matrix & Governing Provision Breakdown
**Primary StatCon Classification:**
**Statutory Construction Area:** Mandatory vs. Directory Words → Statutory Imperatives → Use of "Shall" and Conjunctive "And" Qualified by a Statutory Proviso → Due Process and Nature of **In Rem** Proceedings.
**Specific Canon / Principle / Rule Applied:** Plain Meaning Rule (**Verba Legis**); Imperative Meaning of the Word "Shall"; Doctrine of Harmonizing Provisos with the Enacting Clause; Strict Construction of Notice Requirements in Actions **In Rem**.
**Specific Latin Maxim: Verba legis non est recedendum** (implicit in the Court’s holding: **"Where the law speaks in clear and categorical language, there is no room for interpretation, vacillation or equivocation; there is room only for application"**).
**Specific Sub-Issue:** Whether the statutory proviso stating that **"publication in the Official Gazette shall be sufficient to confer jurisdiction upon the court"** renders the concomitant requirement that notice **shall** be published **"and once in a newspaper of general circulation"** merely directory or dispensable.
**The Contested Statutory / Constitutional Text (Verbatim):**
**Section 23, Presidential Decree No. 1529 (Property Registration Decree):**
"Sec. 23. **Notice of initial hearing, publication, etc.** — The court **shall**, within five days from filing of the application, issue an order setting the date and hour of the initial hearing which shall not be earlier than forty-five days nor later than ninety days from the date of the order.
The public **shall** be given notice of initial hearing of the application for land registration by means of (1) publication; (2) mailing; and (3) posting.
1. By publication. —
Upon receipt of the order of the court setting the time for initial hearing, the Commissioner of Land Registration **shall cause a notice of initial hearing to be published once in the Official Gazette and once in a newspaper of general circulation in the Philippines: Provided, however, that the publication in the Official Gazette shall be sufficient to confer jurisdiction upon the court.** Said notice **shall** be addressed to all persons appearing to have an interest in the land involved including the adjoining owners so far as known, and 'to all whom it may concern.' Said notice **shall** also require all persons concerned to appear in court at a certain date and time to show cause why the prayer of said application shall not be granted.
x x x           x x x           x x x"
**Historical / Amendment Tracking:**
**Historical Context:** P.D. No. 1529 (promulgated June 11, 1978) updated and codified the land registration laws, superseding Act No. 496 (The Land Registration Act of 1902). Under Act No. 496, publication was similarly rooted in notice to the whole world, but P.D. No. 1529 explicitly inserted the dual requirement of publication in the Official Gazette **and** in a newspaper of general circulation, appended with the proviso regarding the jurisdictional effect of Official Gazette publication.
**StatCon Diagnostic Profile:**
**The Linguistic / Interpretive Defect:** Latent Ambiguity arising from an apparent internal conflict between the mandatory command (**"shall cause a notice... to be published once in the Official Gazette and once in a newspaper of general circulation"**) and the statutory proviso (**"Provided, however, that the publication in the Official Gazette shall be sufficient to confer jurisdiction upon the court"**).
**Was Statutory Construction Legally Permissible?:** Yes, to ascertain whether the imperative word "shall" was modified by the jurisdictional proviso into a directory clause. However, once harmonized with the due process clause and the nature of **in rem** proceedings, the Court held that the command was plain and categorical, leaving **"no room for interpretation, vacillation or equivocation; there is room only for application."**
**Controlling Canon / Maxim Deployed:** The imperative rule on statutory "shall" (denoting an obligatory command); the rule of parity of reasoning within the same section (**Republic v. Marasigan**); the Plain Meaning Rule (**Verba Legis**).
**Factual Interpretive Trigger:** An applicant for land registration published notice of the initial hearing exclusively in the Official Gazette, completely omitting publication in a newspaper of general circulation, prompting the trial court to dismiss the application while the appellate court excused the omission as a mere non-fatal procedural defect.
3. Cast of Characters & Procedural Posture
**Key Parties & Roles:**
**The Director of Lands:** Petitioner; represented by the Office of the Solicitor General (OSG); opposed the registration and challenged the validity of the proceedings due to lack of newspaper publication.
**Teodoro Abistado:** Original applicant for original land registration under P.D. No. 1529 over 648 square meters of land in Poblacion Mamburao, Occidental Mindoro.
**Margarita, Marissa, Maribel, Arnold, and Mary Ann Abistado:** Private respondents; children and legal heirs substituting the deceased Teodoro Abistado, represented by their aunt and guardian **ad litem**, Josefa Abistado.
**Commissioner of Land Registration:** Public official statutorily charged under Section 23 of P.D. No. 1529 with causing the publication of notice in both the Official Gazette and a newspaper of general circulation.
**Procedural History & Vehicle:**
**Trial Court (Branch 44, Regional Trial Court of Mamburao, Occidental Mindoro; LRC No. 86):** In its Decision dated June 13, 1989, the trial court dismissed the application for want of jurisdiction, ruling that compliance with Section 23(1) of P.D. No. 1529 requiring newspaper publication is mandatory.
**Court of Appeals (Seventh Division; CA-G.R. CV No. 23719):** In its Decision dated July 3, 1991 and Resolution dated November 19, 1991, the CA reversed the RTC, holding that newspaper publication was merely procedural and non-jurisdictional under the proviso of Section 23(1), and confirmed title in favor of private respondents.
**Supreme Court (Rule 45 Review):** The Solicitor General originally styled the petition under Rule 65, but the Supreme Court treated it as a Petition for Review on Certiorari under Rule 45 to review a final judgment of the CA. The Supreme Court reversed the Court of Appeals and reinstated the dismissal of the application without prejudice.
### 4. Chronological Facts Storyboard
1. **December 8, 1986:** Teodoro Abistado filed an application for original registration of title under P.D. No. 1529 over a 648-square-meter parcel of land (covered by MSI (IV-A-8) 315-D) situated in Barangay 7, Poblacion Mamburao, Occidental Mindoro, docketed as LRC No. 86 before the RTC of Mamburao, Branch 44.
2. **Pendency of Proceedings:** Applicant Teodoro Abistado died and was substituted by his heirs (Margarita, Marissa, Maribel, Arnold, and Mary Ann Abistado), represented by their guardian **ad litem**, Josefa Abistado.
3. **Publication Process:** Notice of the initial hearing (Exhibit "E") was issued and published in two consecutive issues of the Official Gazette (Exhibits "F" and "G"). However, **no publication was ever made in a newspaper of general circulation**. Personal notice by mailing and posting were executed.
4. **June 13, 1989:** The RTC dismissed the petition for "want of jurisdiction." While noting that applicants had established open, continuous, exclusive, and peaceful possession since 1938, it held that failure to publish in a newspaper of general circulation pursuant to Section 23(1) of P.D. No. 1529 and Ministry of Justice Opinion No. 48 (Series of 1982) was a fatal defect violating mandatory due process.
5. **July 3, 1991:** On appeal, the Court of Appeals set aside the RTC's dismissal and granted the land registration, ruling that Section 23 explicitly makes publication in the Official Gazette sufficient to confer jurisdiction, rendering newspaper publication a non-prejudicial procedural requirement.
6. **November 19, 1991:** The CA denied the Motion for Reconsideration filed by the Director of Lands.
7. **Petition to the Supreme Court:** The Director of Lands, through the Solicitor General, elevated the matter to the Supreme Court.
5. Competing Interpretations Matrix (The Clash of Canons)
A. Petitioner's Interpretation (Director of Lands / Republic)
**Core Reading:** Section 23 of P.D. No. 1529 explicitly requires that notice of initial hearing be published **both** in the Official Gazette **and** in a newspaper of general circulation. The two forms of publication serve dual, non-dispensable requirements: Official Gazette publication confers jurisdiction upon the court, while newspaper publication satisfies the constitutional and procedural demands of due process.
**Canons, Aids, & Maxims Invoked:**
**Plain Meaning & Imperative Word "Shall":** The statute uses "shall," which denotes an obligatory command admitting of no discretion.
**Administrative Construction:** Ministry of Justice Opinion No. 48, Series of 1982, stating that both forms of publication are indispensably necessary—one for statutory jurisdiction, the other for procedural due process.
**Conjunctive Meaning of "And":** The word "and" couples the two publication modes as concurrent necessities.
**Policy / Consequence Argument:** Land registration is an action **in rem** resulting in a decree binding against the whole world. Because the Official Gazette has limited circulation and is frequently delayed, dispensing with newspaper publication deprives unknown claimants and the public of constructive notice, violating procedural due process.
B. Respondent's Interpretation (Abistado Heirs & Court of Appeals)
**Core Reading:** Under the express statutory proviso of Section 23(1), publication in the Official Gazette is legally sufficient to vest jurisdiction in the land registration court. Omission of newspaper publication is a mere "procedural defect" that does not invalidate the proceedings or strip the court of authority to adjudicate title.
**Canons, Aids, & Maxims Invoked:**
**Express Statutory Proviso: "Provided, however, that the publication in the Official Gazette shall be sufficient to confer jurisdiction upon the court."**
**Substantial Compliance / Lack of Prejudice:** Oppositors appeared and actively participated; thus, the purpose of notice was achieved without prejudice.
**Policy / Consequence Argument:** Applying the newspaper requirement strictly creates an unnecessary technical barrier that defeats substantive justice, especially where open, peaceful, and continuous possession since 1938 was conclusively proven.
6. Inventory of Statutory Construction & Substantive Issues
### 1. [PRIMARY STATCON ISSUE]
**Faithful Court Formulation:** "Is newspaper publication of the notice of initial hearing in an original land registration case mandatory or directory?"
**Recit-Ready StatCon Question:** Whether the requirement in Section 23(1) of P.D. No. 1529 that notice of initial hearing "shall" be published in a newspaper of general circulation is mandatory or merely directory, in light of the proviso that publication in the Official Gazette "shall be sufficient to confer jurisdiction upon the court."
2. [Procedural Issue]
**Faithful Court Formulation:** Whether an appeal from a final decision of the Court of Appeals filed by the Solicitor General as a petition for certiorari under Rule 65 should be dismissed or treated as a petition for review under Rule 45.
### 7. Deep-Dive Verdict, Tool Analysis, & Ratio Decidendi per Issue
Issue 1: Mandatory Character of Newspaper Publication under Section 23, P.D. No. 1529
**(a) Short Answer: YES.** Newspaper publication is **mandatory**. While publication in the Official Gazette suffices to confer jurisdiction, the statutory command that notice "shall" also be published in a newspaper of general circulation is an indispensable imperative grounded in procedural due process for **in rem** proceedings.
**(b) Verbatim Doctrinal & Canons Pronouncements:**
"The law used the term 'shall' in prescribing the work to be done by the Commissioner of Land Registration upon the latter's receipt of the court order setting the time for initial hearing. The said word denotes an imperative and thus indicates the mandatory character of a statute."
"Indeed, if mailing of notices is essential, then by parity of reasoning, publication in a newspaper of general circulation is likewise imperative since the law included such requirement in its detailed provision."
"Admittedly, there was failure to comply with the explicit publication requirement of the law. Private respondents did not proffer any excuse; even if they had, it would not have mattered because the statute itself allows no excuses. Ineludibly, this Court has no authority to dispense with such mandatory requirement. The law is unambiguous and its rationale clear. Time and again, this Court has declared that where the law speaks in clear and categorical language, there is no room for interpretation, vacillation or equivocation; there is room only for application."
**(c) Step-by-Step Interpretative Reasoning:**
1. **Threshold Gate:** The Court rejected the appellate court's position that the proviso subordinated newspaper publication to a mere directory formality. It recognized that while the text explicitly concedes jurisdiction upon Official Gazette publication, the statute **categorically commands** newspaper publication through unambiguous mandatory language. Thus, **verba legis** applies: there is no room for judicial dispensation.
2. Intrinsic Aids Examined:
**Grammatical / Lexical Meaning of "Shall":** The word "shall" in Section 23 governs the Commissioner's duty to publish both in the Official Gazette and in a newspaper. In statutory construction, "shall" normally denotes an imperative command rather than a permissive or directory suggestion.
**Harmonizing the Proviso with the Enacting Clause:** The proviso (**"Provided, however, that the publication in the Official Gazette shall be sufficient to confer jurisdiction..."**) establishes the baseline for subject-matter/res jurisdiction, but does not eviscerate the primary enacting mandate requiring publication in a newspaper. The two requirements coexist: one addresses jurisdiction, the other fulfills the statutory notice mechanism of due process.
**Contextual Parity (**Republic v. Marasigan**):** Section 23 provides three cumulative methods of notice: publication, mailing, and posting. Since prior jurisprudence held that detailed mailing requirements to adjoining owners cannot be dispensed with, by parity of reasoning, newspaper publication explicitly embedded in the statute must equally be complied with.
3. Extrinsic Aids Examined:
The Court observed the practical reality of public dissemination: the Official Gazette has limited circulation and is frequently delayed in publication and distribution. Relying on it alone denies effective constructive notice to unknown parties, adjoining owners, or ordinary citizens.
4. Statutory Presumptions & Policies (Nature of In Rem Proceedings):
Land registration is a proceeding **in rem**, which demands constructive seizure of the land against the entire world.
To bar the rights of all potential claimants validly under constitutional due process, notice must be disseminated as widely as the law prescribes. The applicant must prove title against the whole world; hence, the statutory publication requirements must be strictly enforced.
5. **Rejection of Losing Construction:** The Court of Appeals' holding that newspaper publication is merely procedural and non-prejudicial was rejected because the statute itself provides no exceptions and allows no excuses. The judiciary has no power to waive an explicit statutory requirement designed to protect third parties and the public from secret land registrations.
**(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation:**
**(Plain-Language StatCon Explanation)** The word "shall" in Section 23 of P.D. 1529 is strictly mandatory, requiring publication in both the Official Gazette and a newspaper of general circulation. Although the law states that Official Gazette publication is sufficient to give the court jurisdiction, newspaper publication is an indispensable requirement of procedural due process in **in rem** proceedings because the Official Gazette is not widely circulated. Because the statutory command is absolute and unambiguous, courts have no authority to dispense with newspaper publication, and failure to comply requires dismissal of the registration application.
Issue 2: Procedural Treatment of Rule 65 Certiorari as Rule 45 Review
**(a) Short Answer: TREATED AS RULE 45.** An erroneous styling of a petition as a special civil action for certiorari under Rule 65 will be treated as an appeal by certiorari under Rule 45 where it seeks to review a final judgment of the Court of Appeals and was timely filed within the requested extension period.
**(b) Verbatim Doctrinal & Canons Pronouncements:**
"This Court notes that the petitioner's counsel anchored his petition on Rule 65. This is an error. His remedy should be based on Rule 45 because he is appealing a final disposition of the Court of Appeals. Hence, we shall treat his petition as one for review under Rule 45, and not for **certiorari** under Rule 65."
**(c) Step-by-Step Interpretative Reasoning:**
1. An appeal from a final decision of the Court of Appeals is properly pursued via a petition for review on certiorari under Rule 45, raising questions of law, not an original action under Rule 65.
2. Because the Solicitor General timely moved for an extension of time to file a petition for review on certiorari and the Court granted the same, the mislabeling in the petition’s text was treated as a formal defect, and the petition was admitted and adjudicated on its legal merits under Rule 45.
**(d) Plain-Language "Recit-Ready" Explanation:**
**(Plain-Language StatCon Explanation)** Even though the government mistakenly labeled its pleading as a Rule 65 petition for certiorari, the Supreme Court treated it as a proper Rule 45 appeal because it sought review of a final judgment of the Court of Appeals and was filed within the allowed period.
8. Separate Opinions on Statutory Construction
**No separate opinions discussed in the provided text.**
9. Overall Verdict (Dispositive Portion / Fallo)
**Verbatim Fallo:**
"WHEREFORE, the petition is GRANTED and the assailed Decision and Resolution are REVERSED and SET ASIDE. The application of private respondent for land registration is DISMISSED without prejudice. No costs.
SO ORDERED."
**Plain-Language Outcome:**
The petitioner (Director of Lands) prevailed. The Supreme Court reversed the Court of Appeals and dismissed the Abistado heirs' application for land registration because they failed to publish notice of the initial hearing in a newspaper of general circulation. However, the dismissal was made **without prejudice**, meaning the heirs may reapply for registration provided they strictly comply with all statutory notice requirements—including newspaper publication—in the new proceeding.
